s1-headline.Breakdown.breakdownOnSpace_of_profile: `Breakdown.breakdownOnSpace_of_profile` proves the nonexistence conclusion on $\mathbb R^3$. From a smooth nonzero recurrent profile with decay through two velocity derivatives and decay of the pressure gradient, it gives compactly supported solenoidal data for each positive viscosity. No global smooth solution for those data has uniformly bounded energy. The trajectory and rate described in Theorem 1.1 require a further result.
s1-headline.Breakdown.Periodic.breakdownOnTorus_of_p: `Breakdown.Periodic.breakdownOnTorus_of_profile` proves the periodic nonexistence conclusion from a smooth nonzero recurrent profile with decay through two velocity derivatives and decay of the pressure gradient. For each positive viscosity the datum is smooth, solenoidal and periodic. Any proposed global smooth solution with periodic velocity is excluded, even with nonperiodic pressure.

s1-profile-reduction.Breakdown.breakdownOnSpace_of_profile: `Breakdown.breakdownOnSpace_of_profile` reduces whole-space breakdown to existence of a smooth nonzero solution of the similarity equations with orthogonal recurrence, uniform velocity decay through order two and uniform pressure-gradient decay. It concludes that compactly supported smooth solenoidal data can prevent global smooth bounded-energy evolution at every positive viscosity.
s1-profile-reduction.Breakdown.Periodic.breakdownOnTorus_of_p: `Breakdown.Periodic.breakdownOnTorus_of_profile` uses the smooth nonzero recurrent profile as an input, including uniform decay of its spatial derivatives through order two and of its pressure gradient. It gives smooth periodic solenoidal data at each positive viscosity for which a global smooth periodic velocity cannot exist.

s1-unforced.Breakdown.IsSmoothSolution: The momentum equation contains viscosity, advection and pressure and has no external force term.

pdf-item-equation-1-1.Breakdown.IsSmoothSolution: At viscosity one, the momentum and incompressibility conditions are exactly (1.1). Smoothness up to time zero and the initial value are also required, with the equations stated at positive times.

s1-domains.Breakdown.BreakdownOnSpace: `Breakdown.BreakdownOnSpace` states the whole-space failure of global smooth bounded-energy evolution. At each positive viscosity it asks for a smooth compactly supported solenoidal datum for which no smooth solution has a single energy bound on $[0,\infty)$. The definition supplies the proposition used by the nonexistence theorem.
s1-domains.Breakdown.BreakdownOnTorus: `Breakdown.BreakdownOnTorus` states the periodic failure of global smooth evolution for some smooth periodic solenoidal datum at every positive viscosity. Periodicity is imposed on the proposed velocity. A proposed pressure may be any smooth pressure satisfying the equations.

s1-finite-codimension-summary.Breakdown.DichotomyHolds: `Breakdown.DichotomyHolds` supplies the finite-rank commuting projection for a compact perturbation of a bounded operator with small norm. Forward powers decay faster on the complement than inverse powers can grow on the projected space. The separation underlies the choice of finitely many corrections to the datum.
s1-finite-codimension-summary.Breakdown.StepDataStatement: `Breakdown.StepDataStatement` packages the bounded linear solve on rescaled intervals. The correction to the datum lies in the image of a fixed finite-dimensional space chosen using the spectral split. The nonlinear stability conclusion uses this solve as an input.

s1-certificate-summary.Breakdown.certificate_orbit: `Breakdown.certificate_orbit` assumes the earlier certificate over a rectangular parameter box and gives a nonzero recurrent weak profile. The smoothness, error bounds and prescribed symmetries described here belong to the stronger conclusion in the paper.

s1-similarity-time.Breakdown.physicalTime: For $t<1$, `Breakdown.physicalTime` gives the similarity time $s=s_0-\log(1-t)$. Setting $s_0=0$ gives the passage’s time coordinate at final time $T=1$.
s1-similarity-time.Breakdown.physicalScale: For $t<1$, `Breakdown.physicalScale` is the factor $(1-t)^{-1/2}$ multiplying $x$ to obtain the similarity position. The paper writes the scaling for general final time $T$.

s1-profile-domain.Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExist: `Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExists` asks for a period $S>0$ and an orthogonal linear isometry $R$ along with the profile. In the paper these are fixed before the recurrence relation is imposed.

s1-profile-smoothness.Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExist: The formal premise uses jointly smooth functions on all real similarity times and on Euclidean three-space and requires $W(s,y)\ne0$ somewhere. The decay and recurrence clauses are separate components of that premise.

pdf-item-equation-1-2.Breakdown.SimilarityResidual: `Breakdown.SimilarityResidual` is the left-hand side of the momentum equation. Its definition alone asserts neither that it vanishes nor that $W$ is divergence-free.
pdf-item-equation-1-2.Breakdown.IsSimilarityProfile: `Breakdown.IsSimilarityProfile` requires the similarity momentum equation and zero divergence for every $(s,y)$, with joint smoothness and uniform velocity decay through order two and pressure-gradient decay. The recurrence involving $S$ and $R$ belongs to the separate existence premise.
pdf-item-equation-1-2.Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExist: `Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExists` includes all three identities in (1.2), with existentially chosen $S>0$ and $R\in O(3)$. It also requires a smooth profile that is nonzero somewhere, with uniform velocity decay through order two and pressure-gradient decay.
pdf-item-equation-1-2.Breakdown.pushForward: `Breakdown.pushForward` defines $RW(s,R^{-1}y)$ for the time slice. It does not itself assert recurrence.

pdf-item-equation-1-3.Breakdown.IsSimilarityProfile: `Breakdown.IsSimilarityProfile` includes the two decay powers in (1.3) and additionally requires the second velocity derivative and pressure gradient to decay like $(1+|y|)^{-3}$. Lean uses operator norms for the derivatives.
pdf-item-equation-1-3.Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExist: `Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExists` builds both bounds (1.3) into the smooth recurrent-profile premise. The same constant also bounds the second velocity derivative and the pressure gradient by multiples of $(1+|y|)^{-3}$, with operator norms for the derivatives.

pdf-item-equation-1-4.Breakdown.physicalField: The formal velocity has final time one and arbitrary phase $s_0$, for phase zero the paper formula is $T^{-1/2}u_1^*(t/T,x/\sqrt T)$.
pdf-item-equation-1-4.Breakdown.MildFramework.selfSimilar: `Breakdown.MildFramework.selfSimilar` defines the change of variables in a Hilbert space with a dilation family $D_\mu$. At zero phase it applies $D_{(1-t)^{-1}}$ to the orbit at $-\log(1-t)$, which gives (1.4) for $T=1$ in the homogeneous $\dot H^1$ realization.

s1-physical-pde.Breakdown.Periodic.selfSimilarSolves: `Breakdown.Periodic.selfSimilarSolves` proves the classical equations and joint smoothness for all $t<T$ with arbitrary $T>0$, but translates the centre to $(1/2,1/2,1/2)$ and assumes the additional derivative and pressure-gradient decay.
s1-physical-pde.Breakdown.physicalPressure: At $T=1$ and zero phase, `Breakdown.physicalPressure` supplies the pressure $(1-t)^{-1}q(s,y)$ accompanying the velocity change of variables. Verification of the physical equations uses a separate result.

adapted.N1-04.1.Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExist: `Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExists` requires the velocity to recur after every shift by $S>0$, up to the orthogonal action. Substituting the paper’s similarity time into that recurrence gives the factor $e^{-S}$ on the remaining physical time and hence the length and speed factors.

pdf-item-equation-1-5.Breakdown.MildFramework.IsOrbit: `Breakdown.MildFramework.IsOrbit` packages recurrence $w(s+S)=\rho_Rw(s)$ with the mild equation in similarity time. Converting this recurrence to (1.5) also uses the physical dilation and the relation $\lambda=e^{-S}$.
pdf-item-equation-1-5.Breakdown.physicalField: `Breakdown.physicalField` supplies the change of variables at final time one, with a freely chosen phase. To recover (1.5), use the recurrent-profile premise and take $\lambda=e^{-S}$, then rescale to the paper’s general $T$.

s1-eulerian-decay.Breakdown.IsSimilarityProfile: In particular, this condition by itself includes the zero field. All denominators are positive because $1+|y|>0$. The derivative bounds are for the three natural-number orders $0,1,2$, rather than for every real order. The pressure-gradient bound and the second-derivative bound are additional explicit assumptions compared with (1.2) and (1.3). The formal bounds are imposed on $W$ in similarity variables and include extra derivative and pressure-gradient decay. These Eulerian bounds require substitution and scaling, with a norm-equivalence factor for the gradient.
s1-eulerian-decay.Breakdown.physicalField: The formal function is defined at every real time. Division by zero and the square root of a nonpositive number are assigned zero, so the defined field is zero for $t\ge1$. No claim of a solution at those times follows. All uses of the change of variables in the evolution restrict to $t<1$. This definition is the required change of variables at final time one. It does not impose the displayed bounds.

s1-smooth-finite-interval.Breakdown.IsSmoothSolution: The linked formal condition is on the entire half-line $[0,\infty)$, with viscosity $\nu$ and the equations imposed at $t>0$. The paper defines solutions on arbitrary finite or infinite intervals.

s1-energy-definition.Breakdown.EnergyBoundedOn: `Breakdown.EnergyBoundedOn` requires one finite upper bound on $\int_{\mathbb R^3}|u(t,x)|^2\,dx$ for all $t\in[0,T]$. It implements the paper’s uniform-in-time energy condition on a specified closed interval.
s1-energy-definition.Breakdown.BreakdownOnSpace: The energy condition inside `Breakdown.BreakdownOnSpace` is one finite upper bound on $\int_{\mathbb R^3}|u(t,x)|^2\,dx$ for every $t\ge0$. This is the global version of the uniform-in-time condition in the passage.

s1-periodic-definition.Breakdown.Periodic.IsPeriodic: `Breakdown.Periodic.IsPeriodic` requires $f(x+e_i)=f(x)$ for every point and each coordinate direction. The function is still represented on $\mathbb R^3$.

s1-periodic-pressure.Breakdown.BreakdownOnTorus: The paper requires periodic velocity and pressure. `Breakdown.BreakdownOnTorus` excludes a larger class of global smooth solutions because it requires periodicity of the velocity alone.

s1-theorem-premise.Breakdown.breakdownOnSpace_of_profile: `Breakdown.breakdownOnSpace_of_profile` assumes a smooth nonzero profile solving the similarity equations and recurring up to an orthogonal map. Its decay premise includes second velocity derivatives and the pressure gradient. It concludes global nonexistence in the smooth bounded-energy class for compactly supported solenoidal data at each positive viscosity. The quantitative whole-space trajectory is proved in the companion Lean under the explicit decay premise.
s1-theorem-premise.Breakdown.Periodic.breakdownOnTorus_of_p: `Breakdown.Periodic.breakdownOnTorus_of_profile` uses the strengthened profile premise, including second velocity derivative and pressure-gradient decay. Its result excludes a global smooth velocity for some smooth periodic datum at each positive viscosity, allowing a nonperiodic pressure. The finite-time periodic trajectory and the local error in (1.7) fall outside this statement.

s1-theorem-space.Breakdown.breakdownOnSpace_of_profile: At each positive viscosity, `Breakdown.breakdownOnSpace_of_profile` gives a smooth compactly supported solenoidal datum from a smooth nonzero recurrent profile with decay of the velocity through order two and of the pressure gradient. Its conclusion excludes smooth global bounded-energy evolution. The companion Lean proves the finite-time trajectory and the physical error bound under the strengthened profile assumptions.
s1-theorem-space.Breakdown.TransferHolds: Under the abstract heat, bilinear and dilation assumptions, `Breakdown.TransferHolds` gives a mild curve with initial datum arbitrarily close to the profile in a chosen dense linear subspace. It bounds the error after dilation in the Hilbert norm. Physical smoothness and finite energy use the whole-space realization.

pdf-item-equation-1-6.Breakdown.TransferHolds: `Breakdown.TransferHolds` gives an error bound after dilation for the abstract mild curve near a recurrent orbit under the heat, bilinear and dilation hypotheses. Converting this to the physical comparison in (1.6) uses the $\dot H^1$ dilation law. The two-sided rate also uses upper and positive lower bounds on the reference orbit.
pdf-item-equation-1-6.Breakdown.orbitNorm: `Breakdown.orbitNorm` supplies the positive lower bound on the norm of a continuous nonzero recurrent mild orbit, with recurrence by an isometry commuting with the evolution and scaling operators. Applying the physical dilation gives the lower rate for the reference flow.
pdf-item-equation-1-6.Breakdown.orbitBound: `Breakdown.orbitBound` bounds the reference orbit uniformly in similarity time by continuity and recurrence under an isometry. After physical dilation this gives the upper $(1-t)^{-1/4}$ rate for the reference flow.

s1-theorem-periodic.Breakdown.Periodic.TorusBlowup: `Breakdown.Periodic.TorusBlowup` describes a continuous mild curve on the unit torus starting at a smooth periodic solenoidal datum and becoming unbounded in $H^1$. The paper states a smooth trajectory with periodic pressure and quantitative estimates to a localized reference flow.

pdf-item-equation-1-7.Breakdown.Periodic.TorusBlowup: `Breakdown.Periodic.TorusBlowup` encodes unboundedness of a periodic mild curve in the inhomogeneous $H^1$ norm. It gives no two-sided power law or error estimate on $B_{1/16}$ of the kind written in (1.7).

s1-rescaled-error.Breakdown.TransferHolds: Put $s=-\log(1-t)$ and $U(s)=D_{1-t}u(t)$, where $D_\mu f(x)=\sqrt\mu f(\sqrt\mu x)$ in the whole-space realization $X=\dot H^1_{\rm div}(\mathbb R^3)$. `Breakdown.TransferHolds` is $\|U(s)-w(s)\|_X\le A e^{-\kappa s}$ for $s\ge0$, with some $A\in\mathbb R$ and $\kappa>0$. Identifying $w(s)$ with $W(s,\cdot)$ gives precisely the displayed gradient-norm error. This row compares that estimate. It does not additionally require $\kappa<1/4$.

s1-unperturbed-rate.Breakdown.Freq.dilation_holds: Although the formal dilation family has values at all real parameters, it is assigned zero for $\mu\le0$ and none of these positive-parameter identities uses those values. These conclusions establish the three identities of (3.5) in the Fourier representation. The dilation norm law is $\|D_\mu f\|=\mu^{1/4}\|f\|$. Taking $\mu=(T-t)^{-1}$ yields the displayed scaling for the homogeneous gradient norm.
s1-unperturbed-rate.Breakdown.orbitNorm: `Breakdown.orbitNorm` is the lower bound on the recurrent orbit. It does not include a nearby solution $u$, the upper bound in (2.5), the chosen constant $c_*/2$, or uniformity over all nearby data $w_0$. Those require the quantitative correction and a separate upper bound for the orbit. For a nonzero recurrent mild orbit in the stated Hilbert setting, it gives one positive lower norm bound for every real similarity time.
s1-unperturbed-rate.Breakdown.orbitBound: `Breakdown.orbitBound` bounds the continuous reference orbit uniformly in similarity time using recurrence by an isometry. The scaling in the passage converts this into the upper gradient rate for $u_T^*$.

s1-nearby-data.Breakdown.ContractionStatement: The formal contraction assertion handles every sufficiently small abstract initial displacement with a correction controlled linearly in its norm. Finite-dimensionality, smooth compact support, physical smoothness and energy require other results.
s1-nearby-data.Breakdown.StepDataStatement: The formal linear right inverse places its initial correction in a fixed finite-dimensional image inside a chosen dense subspace. It does not by itself prove nonlinear blow-up.
s1-nearby-data.Breakdown.TransferHolds: For every dense real linear subspace $C\subset X$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, the conclusion chooses a datum $u(0)\in C$ with $\|u(0)-w(0)\|<\varepsilon$ and a continuous mild curve on $[0,1)$. For some $A\in\mathbb R$ and $\kappa>0$, it satisfies $\|D_{1-t}u(t)-w(-\log(1-t))\|\le A(1-t)^\kappa$ for every $0\le t<1$. Here mildness means $u(t)=G(t)u(0)+\int_0^tK(t-r)(u(r),u(r))\,dr$, with each Bochner integral convergent. The datum is chosen after the dense subspace and tolerance. The assertion does not start from every prescribed nearby $w_0$ or retain a fixed finite-dimensional correction space, which are the quantifiers in the paper's finite-codimension statement.

s1-remark-decay.Breakdown.IsSimilarityProfile: In particular, this condition by itself includes the zero field. All denominators are positive because $1+|y|>0$. The derivative bounds are for the three natural-number orders $0,1,2$, rather than for every real order. The pressure-gradient bound and the second-derivative bound are additional explicit assumptions compared with (1.2) and (1.3). `Breakdown.IsSimilarityProfile` assumes decay through two spatial derivatives and pressure-gradient decay. It does not prove this implication from velocity decay alone, and its derivative bounds use operator norms.

s1-minimal-profile-premise.Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExist: Remark 1.2 derives the first- and second-derivative velocity bounds from the velocity bound and the equations. It does not state the pressure-gradient bound. This formal statement therefore cannot be cited as the reduction to the velocity-only hypothesis, and the cited remark alone does not settle every extra formal premise.

s1-certificate-assumes-profile.Breakdown.certificate_orbit: `Breakdown.certificate_orbit` assumes the earlier certificate form and concludes a nonzero recurrent weak profile. Smoothness, prescribed symmetry and pointwise decay are not asserted in this conclusion.

s1-certificate-family.Breakdown.certificate_orbit: The formal premise contains such data over a rectangular parameter box, with unit weight on forcing coefficients and a local ball norm. The current paper uses a more general parameter set, forcing weight and reference-profile estimate.

s1-certificate-universal-estimates.Breakdown.certificate_orbit: The formal certificate premise includes an estimate quantified over every symmetry-invariant weak perturbation, every finite forcing coefficient vector and every square-integrable periodic right-hand side satisfying the linearized equation.

s1-certificate-smooth-conclusion.Breakdown.certificate_orbit: `Breakdown.certificate_orbit` is existence of some recurrent weak profile. It does not identify the orthogonal map as the identity, preserve the chosen symmetry data in the statement, or provide the closeness estimate.

s1-certificate-numerical-inequalities.Breakdown.certificate_orbit: The formal premise requires residual bounds, three smallness inequalities, nontriviality and parameter inclusion inequalities. The theorem does not provide or check a numerical instance of them.

s1-symmetry-class.Breakdown.certificate_orbit: The coercive estimate in the formal premise is quantified over perturbations invariant under every prescribed orthogonal map and accompanying time shift. The frozen quadratic form uses the purely spatial symmetries.

s1-outline-base-solution.Breakdown.Periodic.selfSimilarSolves: `Breakdown.Periodic.selfSimilarSolves` supplies the classical unforced solution for a translated centre and the stronger smooth-profile premise. The perturbative construction is a further theorem.
s1-outline-base-solution.Breakdown.TransferHolds: `Breakdown.TransferHolds` gives the abstract mild curve near a recurrent orbit under the Hilbert-space heat, bilinear, dilation and compactness hypotheses. Its datum is arbitrarily close to the profile in a chosen dense linear subspace. To interpret it as a smooth finite-energy physical solution, the argument uses the whole-space realization and its regularity theorem.

adapted.N1-12.1.Breakdown.Freq.gradSixDecay: For smooth decaying fields, `Breakdown.Freq.gradSixDecay` places the velocity in $L^6$ and its gradient in $L^2$ using the spatial decay hypotheses. Since the constants in (1.3) are uniform in $s$, the estimates on the profile slices are uniform too.

s1-outline-regularity.Breakdown.MildRegular: `Breakdown.MildRegular` states the whole-space regularity property for a mild curve through compactly supported smooth solenoidal data. On each shorter closed interval it yields a smooth physical representative, with uniform energy, velocity and gradient bounds. Torus regularity uses a separate periodic result.

s1-outline-torus-space.Breakdown.Periodic.V: A nonzero constant has positive formal norm and zero gradient norm, so the mean-zero restriction is essential in (3.16). Equation (3.15) instead uses the homogeneous norm on mean-zero fields of arbitrary period $L$. The distinction matters: the zero Fourier mode contributes to the formal norm, and no variable spatial period is a parameter of an element of the formal space. The formal unit-torus space uses the inhomogeneous $H^1$ weight $1+4\pi^2|k|^2$ and retains the zero Fourier coefficient. Mean zero is not part of that space definition.

s1-outline-similarity-equation.Breakdown.SimilarityResidual: Nor does the definition itself assume differentiability: derivative operations have assigned values where a classical derivative does not exist. In every smooth-profile application the smoothness hypotheses ensure that all terms are the ordinary derivatives appearing in (1.2). The spatial Laplacian is the sum of the pure second derivatives, and the spatial derivative of $W$ applied to $y$ is $(y\cdot\nabla)W$. `Breakdown.SimilarityResidual` records the similarity momentum equation, but the definition alone does not prove equivalence under the change of variables.
s1-outline-similarity-equation.Breakdown.physicalField: `Breakdown.physicalField` defines $u(t,x)=(1-t)^{-1/2}U(s,y)$ when $t<1$ and the phase is zero. Substitution into the differential equations requires smoothness and uses the derivatives of the time and space change.

adapted.N1-13.1.Breakdown.Freq.dilation_holds: `Breakdown.Freq.dilation_holds` proves that the homogeneous gradient norm scales by $\mu^{1/4}$ under $u(x)\mapsto\sqrt\mu\,u(\sqrt\mu x)$. For $\mu=(1-t)^{-1}$ the derivative contributes $(1-t)^{-1}$ and the square root of the volume factor contributes $(1-t)^{3/4}$.

s1-outline-monodromy.Breakdown.MonodromyStatement: `Breakdown.MonodromyStatement` gives invertibility of $I-A_n$ and $\|(I-A_n)^{-1}\|\le4/3$. Put $\Gamma x(t)=G(t)x$, $Lv=D_\lambda v(h)$, and $M_n=L(I-A_n)^{-1}\Gamma$. It gives $M_{n+k}=\rho M_n\rho^{-1}$, compactness of $\rho^{-1}M_{k-1}\cdots M_0-\rho^{-1}(D_\lambda G(h))^k$, and $\|\rho^{-1}(D_\lambda G(h))^k\|\le e^{-S/4}$. For $k=1$, $(I-A_0)^{-1}\Gamma\chi$ is the solution $h_\chi$ of (4.9) on $[0,t_1]$ and $\rho^{-1}M_0$ is exactly $\mathcal M$ of (4.10). For larger $k$ the product computes the same period map over $k$ shorter steps. It does not state that identity. The subdivision and the bound $\|A_n\|\le1/4$ are explicit hypotheses, where the paper solves (4.9) by Lemma 3.4.

s1-outline-free-flow.Breakdown.Freq.heat_holds: Continuity is strong continuity for each fixed input, including the endpoint $0$. No continuity in operator norm at $0$ is asserted. Negative parameters use the identity extension and are outside the forward semigroup law. The formal heat result gives contraction at nonnegative physical times. The additional dilation norm law produces the factor $e^{-s/4}$.
s1-outline-free-flow.Breakdown.Freq.dilation_holds: Although the formal dilation family has values at all real parameters, it is assigned zero for $\mu\le0$ and none of these positive-parameter identities uses those values. These conclusions establish the three identities of (3.5) in the Fourier representation. The dilation factor at $\mu=e^{-s}$ is $e^{-s/4}$. Applying the heat contraction gives the stated bound for $s\ge0$.

s1-outline-subcritical.Breakdown.dilateField: The formal dilation is $D_\mu f(x)=\sqrt\mu f(\sqrt\mu x)$ for $\mu>0$.
s1-outline-subcritical.Breakdown.Freq.dilation_holds: The formal norm law is exactly the factor $\mu^{1/4}$ for positive dilation parameters.

adapted.N1-15.1.Breakdown.DichotomyHolds: `Breakdown.DichotomyHolds` states the power bounds on either side of the chosen decay rate. Its finite-rank projection separates directions where reverse evolution is controlled from the complement whose forward powers decay faster.

s1-outline-no-spectrum-assumption.Breakdown.DichotomyHolds: The formal hypothesis requires only a compact perturbation of an operator with a norm bound. No prescribed unstable eigenvalue or spectral sign is assumed.

s1-outline-weighted-perturbations.Breakdown.StepDataStatement: `Breakdown.StepDataStatement` uses a weight $\theta$ for each of the $k$ subintervals of a period $S$, with $e^{-S/(4k)}<\theta<1$. Boundedness after division by $\theta^n$ sets the decay rate for the interval corrections. The full-period weight is $\theta^k$.

adapted.N1-15.2.Breakdown.discreteDichotomy: `Breakdown.discreteDichotomy` solves the projected part of the forced recurrence by summing future sources with inverse powers of the projected period map. The power bounds make the series converge and select the initial component with the required decay.

adapted.N1-15.3.Breakdown.exists_section: `Breakdown.exists_section` lifts a basis of the range of a finite-rank bounded projection into a chosen dense linear subspace and extends the lifts linearly. The paper chooses smooth compactly supported solenoidal fields as that subspace.

s1-outline-contraction-nearby.Breakdown.ContractionStatement: The formal contraction handles every small initial displacement in the abstract sequence problem. The finite-dimensional correction space and the identification with a continuous-time mild solution come from separate ingredients.
s1-outline-contraction-nearby.Breakdown.TransferHolds: `Breakdown.TransferHolds` gives a mild solution arbitrarily near the initial point of a recurrent orbit in any chosen dense linear subspace. Its rescaled error decays at a positive power. The paper fixes a finite-dimensional set of correction directions to handle each nearby datum.

s1-outline-fixed-time.Breakdown.TransferHolds: `Breakdown.TransferHolds` compares its constructed mild curve to the prescribed recurrent orbit evaluated at $-\log(1-t)$, with final time fixed at one. The error is measured after dilation, and time, spatial and phase modulation are absent from the conclusion.

s1-outline-vector-potential.Breakdown.Periodic.homotopyPotential: In the paper the centre is the origin. The formal formula permits any centre. This definition alone neither assumes $\operatorname{div}g=0$ nor proves $\operatorname{curl}A=g$. The latter identity requires the separate smoothness and divergence-free hypotheses. No decay at spatial infinity is needed to define this finite radial integral for smooth $g$. At centre zero, the formal radial vector potential has the formula used for $A$. The statement also allows an arbitrary centre.
s1-outline-vector-potential.Breakdown.Periodic.cutoffField: When $\chi$ and $g$ are smooth and $g$ is solenoidal, the identity $\operatorname{curl}A_{x_0,g}=g$ and the product rule identify this definition with $\operatorname{curl}(\chi A_{x_0,g})$. The definition itself requires none of these hypotheses and asserts neither smoothness nor support. Derivatives and the integral are total operations: a derivative is zero where the required derivative does not exist, and a nonintegrable integral is zero. The smoothness hypotheses in the applications eliminate these conventions. The formal cutoff is $\chi g+\nabla\chi\times A$, which equals $\operatorname{curl}(\chi A)$ for a smooth solenoidal field and its vector potential.
s1-outline-vector-potential.Breakdown.Periodic.cutoffDivergenceFree: Assuming the proved radial-potential identity, `Breakdown.Periodic.cutoffDivergenceFree` preserves smoothness and zero divergence for every smooth scalar cutoff.

s1-outline-cutoff-error.Breakdown.Periodic.approxFieldProperties: `Breakdown.Periodic.approxFieldProperties_holds` gives support in radius $1/8$ and agreement in radius $1/16$ about the centre $(1/2,1/2,1/2)$ on the unit cell. It uses a variable final time rather than an arbitrary physical cutoff radius.
s1-outline-cutoff-error.Breakdown.Periodic.cutoffGradientClose: Under the smooth profile equations and the full profile decay hypotheses, `Breakdown.Periodic.cutoffGradientClose` makes the squared gradient error of the rescaled cutoff as small as desired when $T-t$ is small enough. The paper’s explicit radius-dependent rate requires a quantitative estimate.

s1-outline-torus-scaling.Breakdown.Periodic.selfSimilarSolves: `Breakdown.Periodic.selfSimilarSolves` proves the physical equations for the reference velocity and pressure from a smooth similarity profile with the formal decay bounds. The result concerns the whole-space fields. The paper subsequently rescales and localizes them for the periodic domain.
s1-outline-torus-scaling.Breakdown.Periodic.TorusBlowup: The final formal condition records some positive time and an unbounded periodic mild trajectory, without the identity $T=L^{-2}$.

s1-outline-torus-approximation.Breakdown.Periodic.approxFieldProperties: The formal cutoff is centred at $(1/2,1/2,1/2)$ on a unit cell, equals the translated profile inside radius $1/16$, and vanishes outside radius $1/8$. The paper first uses radii proportional to $L$.

s1-outline-kernel-decay.Breakdown.FarField.lerayKernelBound_hold: A norm bound for the entire first derivative follows by summing finitely many components and changing the constant. The exponent $4$ is a fixed natural-number power, and $|x|+\sqrt\tau>0$ under the hypothesis. The paper's (3.9) allows every nonnegative integer derivative order $l$, with a constant depending on $l$. `Breakdown.FarField.lerayKernelBound_holds` gives its first-derivative case only. The formal kernel estimate is $C(|x|+\sqrt\tau)^{-4}$ for all $\tau>0$ and all $x$, which implies the stated time-uniform $C|x|^{-4}$ estimate away from the origin.

s1-outline-torus-final.Breakdown.Periodic.SeqPerturbation: `Breakdown.Periodic.SeqPerturbation` constructs exact mild solutions on rescaled torus intervals from a bounded linear right inverse, sufficiently small residual and datum displacement, and the endpoint matching hypotheses. Recovering the physical flow from these pieces requires the joining and scaling steps.
s1-outline-torus-final.Breakdown.Periodic.TorusBlowup: The formal target retains a unit-periodic mild trajectory with unbounded $H^1$ norm, without the paper's explicit rescaling formula or quantitative bounds.

s1-outline-certificate-force.Breakdown.certificate_orbit: The formal certificate has $n$ forcing fields and $n$ gradient-pairing constraints. Its coercive estimate includes the Euclidean norm of the $n$ unknown forcing coefficients.

s1-background-main-conclusion.Breakdown.breakdownOnSpace_of_profile: `Breakdown.breakdownOnSpace_of_profile` applies the authors’ localization argument on $\mathbb R^3$. Its premise is a smooth nonzero recurrent similarity profile with velocity decay through two derivatives and pressure-gradient decay. Its conclusion is global nonexistence among smooth bounded-energy solutions for some compactly supported smooth solenoidal datum at each positive viscosity.
