It asserts neither a vanishing integral nor an equivalence of periods. Those assertions require separate hypotheses and results.

ns7-data-s007.Breakdown.IsTimePeriodic: The formal period-one condition is the pointwise identity on the full real time axis.

ns7-data-s008.Breakdown.IsPerturbation: The formal domain gives weak spatial derivatives and the distributional combined time-and-dilation derivative explicitly. It does not define every distributional derivative as a separate field.

ns7-data-s009.Breakdown.Cert.IsPeriodicField: `Breakdown.Cert.IsPeriodicField` supplies the vector-valued period-square-integrable representatives. It does not define the matrix-valued Hilbert space.
ns7-data-s009.Breakdown.periodPairing: The period pairing integrates $F\cdot G$ over one normalized time period and all of $\mathbb R^3$. It equals the Hilbert inner product for square-integrable fields. The time endpoints have measure zero.
ns7-data-s009.Breakdown.periodNorm: The spacetime norm is the square root of the integral of $|F|^2$ over one time period and $\mathbb R^3$. The norm formula agrees with the paper when the integral is finite.
ns7-data-s009.Breakdown.matSq: For a matrix $A$ the squared Frobenius norm is the sum $\sum_i|Ae_i|^2$ over the coordinate directions. This is the convention used when the period norm is applied to a derivative matrix.

ns7-data-s010.Breakdown.Cert.HH: `Breakdown.Cert.HH` represents the periodic solenoidal Hilbert space in Fourier variables.
ns7-data-s010.Breakdown.Cert.exists_projSpec: `Breakdown.Cert.exists_projSpec` constructs the spatial Fourier multiplier. Its extension in time and orthogonal-projection properties are separate.

ns7-data-s011.Breakdown.Cert.physToHH: On square-integrable period-one fields this map applies the spatial Leray projection at almost every time.

ns7-data-s012.Breakdown.IsSpaceTimeTestField: The tests are smooth, compactly supported and divergence-free, so a gradient contribution has zero pairing under the requisite integrability.

ns7-data-s013.Breakdown.IsSpaceTimeTestField: `Breakdown.IsSpaceTimeTestField` gives the exact test class in (7.2). It does not define or prove the general relation between arbitrary locally integrable $F$ and $G$.
ns7-data-s013.Breakdown.sigmaSimilarityIntegrand: `Breakdown.sigmaSimilarityIntegrand` gives the particular weak similarity equation, with its derivatives integrated by parts. It has no independent predicate for the general relation $F\simeq G$.

ns7-data-s014.Breakdown.Cert.testPairingHolds_proof: The pairing identity transfers physical tests to the projected periodic field. Separation is needed for the converse.
ns7-data-s014.Breakdown.Cert.testDenseHolds_proof: `Breakdown.Cert.testDenseHolds_proof` says those tests separate the projected field. Together with the pairing identity it yields the stated equivalence.

ns7-data-s016.Breakdown.IsPerturbation: `Breakdown.IsPerturbation` is the formal specification of the admissible weak perturbations, including their time-dilation derivative.

ns7-data-s017.Breakdown.IsPerturbation: The formal conditions encode the domain using weak gradient, weak Hessian and combined time-dilation fields, with finite period integrals. They do not assert the equivalence with the paper’s direct definition as one theorem.

ns7-data-s018.Breakdown.IsPerturbation: Only the combined time-and-dilation field is required to be square integrable. Neither summand is separately required to have that property.

`Breakdown.Cert.Internal.FreeEnergyLocal.exists_energyCurve` supplies a continuous homogeneous-$H^1$ representative for constructed free inverse solutions. It does not identify every physical member of $\mathcal D_S$ with one of those solutions.

ns7-data-s020.Breakdown.Symmetry: The data allow an arbitrary set of orthogonal-map and time-shift pairs, including the empty set.

ns7-data-s021.Breakdown.Symmetry: A symmetry is exactly an orthogonal linear map of $\mathbb R^3$ paired with a real time shift.

ns7-data-s022.Breakdown.IsPerturbation.invariant: For each $(R,\theta_0)\in\Gamma$, Lean writes the weak perturbation symmetry as $v(\theta+\theta_0,Ry)=Rv(\theta,y)$ almost everywhere. Replacing $y$ by $R^{-1}y$ gives (7.5).

ns7-data-s023.Breakdown.Cert.invariantHH: The invariant solenoidal space is the intersection of kernels of the time shift minus the orthogonal action, one for each element of $\Gamma$. Its definition concerns the subspace, with the half-period rule for $m$ supplied separately.
ns7-data-s023.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.twist_me: For a set $\Gamma\subset O(3)\times\mathbb R$, `Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.twist_mem` permits $m=1$ unconditionally and permits $m=2$ when $(R,1/2)\in\Gamma$ for some $R$. Equation (7.6) instead requires $m=2$ whenever such a pair exists. Every choice prescribed by the paper satisfies it. The converse fails when a half-period symmetry is present and $m=1$.

ns7-data-s024.Breakdown.Cert.invariantHH: A solenoidal field lies in this intersection precisely when shifting time by $\theta_0$ gives the same field as acting spatially by $R$, for each $(R,\theta_0)\in\Gamma$. Each condition is imposed by a kernel of a bounded linear operator.

ns7-data-s025.Breakdown.Cert.extendedInvarianceHolds_o: `Breakdown.Cert.extendedInvarianceHolds_of` establishes invariance of the projected convection, quadratic term, forces and residual for certificate data. It does not collect all the commutation identities for arbitrary fields in this sentence.

ns7-data-s026.Breakdown.Cert.invariantHH: The fixed subspace is an intersection of kernels of bounded linear differences, hence closed.
ns7-data-s026.Breakdown.Cert.extendedInvarianceHolds_o: The projection of convection and forcing combinations in the certificate preserves the prescribed time shifts and orthogonal actions. The result is specialized to those combinations in the solenoidal space.

ns7-data-s027.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.params: `Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.params` specifies the interval-and-scaled-ball set immediately. Its compactness and convexity need the sign and nonzero-scale hypotheses.

ns7-data-s028.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.profil: The supplied family has parameter, real time and three-dimensional spatial arguments as stated.
ns7-data-s028.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.period: The period is supplied as a real function of the parameter.

ns7-data-s029.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.period_p: The period is positive at every admissible parameter.
ns7-data-s029.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.period_l: The field requires $S(\alpha)\le S_{\max}$ for every admissible $\alpha$, with one upper bound for the whole parameter set. Continuity and positivity of the period are separate conditions.

ns7-data-s030.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.profile_: The formal hypothesis requires a global $C^1$ map of parameters, time and space, including parameter derivatives and an extension beyond $\mathcal K$.

ns7-data-s031.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.profile_: The formal periodicity is required for all real parameters, extending the paper’s quantifier on $\mathcal K$.
Divergence vanishes at every point for each admissible parameter.
ns7-data-s031.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.profileS: A chosen weak Hessian is identified at every time, with further measurability and decay hypotheses.
ns7-data-s031.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.profile_: For each admissible $\alpha$ the approximate velocity obeys $W_\alpha^{\mathrm a}(\theta+\theta_0,Ry)=R W_\alpha^{\mathrm a}(\theta,y)$ for every prescribed symmetry and every point. This is the symmetry of the approximate velocity, before the correction.
The formal gradient uses operator norm and the same constant need not bound the paper’s Frobenius norm. A uniform weak-Hessian bound is also added.
ns7-data-s031.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.actuator: The actuator family has a single bound on the sum of its squared spacetime norms over one period. This controls the forcing produced by any coefficient vector through Cauchy–Schwarz.
ns7-data-s031.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.multipli: The approximate force coefficient map is continuous on $\mathcal K$.
ns7-data-s031.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.defect: The formal residual is a prescribed differential expression with a supplied gradient contribution, rather than an arbitrary representative modulo gradients.

ns7-data-s032.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.defect_l: The full supplied residual is square integrable before projection. Its chosen gradient contribution participates in the norm.
ns7-data-s032.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.pressure: The formal gradient ambiguity is expressed by annihilation of solenoidal tests, without a scalar pressure variable.

ns7-data-s033.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.defect: The residual definition imposes no continuity in the parameter and no invariance of its raw representative.
ns7-data-s033.Breakdown.Cert.extendedDataContinuityHol: What is proved is continuity of fixed solenoidal test pairings, which is consistent with the absence of residual norm continuity.

ns7-data-s035.Breakdown.pinValue: For a period-one velocity with square-integrable weak gradient and a square-integrable constraint matrix, the formal scalar is $\int_0^1\int\sum_j(Ge_j)\cdot(\Xi e_j)$. Its matrix coordinates put vector component first, while the paper puts derivative direction first. Identifying both supplied matrices with the transposes of the paper’s matrices gives exactly $\ell_i(v)=\langle\nabla v,\Xi_i\rangle_{\mathcal H}$. Applying this scalar to each $i$ gives (7.11).
ns7-data-s035.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.target: The formal data start with complete-field targets and subtract the approximate profile’s constraint to obtain $\bar\ell$.
ns7-data-s035.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.pin_fini: The formal constraint fields have a finite square integral on one period and are read on the time circle. No separate periodicity condition is imposed on their original time-line representatives.

ns7-data-s036.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.IsHeld: `Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.IsHeldSolution` uses the free inverse and the projected equation, adds both correction bounds, and measures coefficients with weight one.
ns7-data-s036.Breakdown.Cert.sliceConvection:
The linearized convection is $(W_\alpha^{\mathrm a}\cdot
abla)v+(v\cdot
abla)W_\alpha^{\mathrm a}$. The quadratic term $(v\cdot
abla)v$ occurs separately in the correction equation.

ns7-data-s037.Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldWeakEquationH: `Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldWeakEquationHolds_of` proves the unforced weak equation when the total coefficients vanish. It does not state the general nonzero-force identity as its conclusion.

ns7-data-s039.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData: The scalar constants are parameter-independent data, while the period, fields, residual bounds and other named maps have their specified parameter arguments.

adapted.N4-01.1.Breakdown.Cert.heldNonzeroHolds_of: `Breakdown.Cert.heldNonzeroHolds_of` uses the lower bound on the approximate profile’s gradient energy over a period and the upper bound on correction energy. These bounds prevent the correction from cancelling the entire profile.

ns7-data-s040.Breakdown.weightedEnergy: The perturbation energy weights the squared gradient and includes the squared Laplacian.

ns7-data-s041.Breakdown.Cert.IsAdmissibleWeight: `Breakdown.Cert.IsAdmissibleWeight` gives exactly boundedness, measurability and the positive lower bound on the spatial weight.
ns7-data-s041.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.multipli: The force coefficient weight is positive.
ns7-data-s041.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.weightFn: The complete formal certificate additionally requires the spatial weight to be invariant under every prescribed orthogonal symmetry.

ns7-data-s042.Breakdown.weightedEnergy: `Breakdown.weightedEnergy` gives the period energy, with Frobenius gradient norm.
ns7-data-s042.Breakdown.Cert.sizeZ: The squared norm of a field and its force coefficients adds the spatially weighted period energy to the squared Euclidean coefficient norm. The coefficient weight is one in this definition. Rescaling the coefficients gives the paper’s weight $\omega$.
ns7-data-s042.Breakdown.supBoundFactor: For positive $w_*$ the scalar is exactly $(4\pi\sqrt{w_*})^{-1/2}$.

ns7-data-s043.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.coercive: `Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.coercive` is the a priori estimate for the reference linearization, assumed uniformly over admissible perturbations.

ns7-data-s044.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.gap_tran: The formal hypothesis bounds the change from reference to approximate convection by the same weighted perturbation norm.

ns7-data-s045.Breakdown.Cert.sliceConvection: With the reference velocity as coefficient, the linearized convection sends $v$ to $(W_\alpha^{\mathrm r}\cdot\nabla)v+(v\cdot\nabla)W_\alpha^{\mathrm r}$. The first term transports the perturbation and the second differentiates the reference field.

ns7-data-s046.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.coercive: `Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.coercive` measures the same right side in its full period norm and in a finite seminorm, with a separate constraint term.

ns7-data-s047.Breakdown.rowNorm: The separate certificate conditions make $e_k$ orthonormal in $\mathcal H$ and require $0\le\tau_k\le c_0^2$. Replacing them by $\sqrt{\tau_k}e_k$ then gives the paper’s fields and seminorm. The definition itself gives no Bessel bound.
ns7-data-s047.Breakdown.Cert.rowNormHolds: After that normalization, `Breakdown.Cert.rowNormHolds` gives the Bessel inequality $[F]\le c_0\|F\|_{\mathcal H}$.

ns7-data-s048.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.coercive: The formal certificate requires $c_2\ge0$, whereas the paper explicitly allows any real $c_2$.

ns7-data-s049.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.coercive: The hypothesis bounds the combined norm of velocity and force coefficients by three quantities. They are the full period norm of the linear right-hand side, its finite row seminorm and the Euclidean norm of the constraints, with the weights from (7.18).

ns7-data-s050.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.coercive: No solenoidality is required of $F$, and its original norm and finite seminorm enter the bound.
ns7-data-s050.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.adjoint_: The adjoint estimate also quantifies over every unprojected square-integrable representative modulo gradients.

ns7-data-s051.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.coercive: The inverse-bound constant is strictly positive.

ns7-data-s053.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.atProf: The construction replaces the reference field by the actual approximate profile and sets the gap to zero. With no forcing rows, the finite row seminorm also vanishes.

ns7-data-s054.Breakdown.weightedEnergy: Since $w\ge w_*>0$, the energy controls the time average of the squared Frobenius gradient norm.
ns7-data-s054.Breakdown.Cert.ProductBoundHolds: The stated bilinear estimate uses the essential supremum of the second factor’s gradient norm as well as the first factor’s weighted energy.

ns7-data-s055.Breakdown.Cert.Internal.ExtendedFrozenBr: `Breakdown.Cert.Internal.ExtendedFrozenBridge.profile_form` gives (7.22) for every real time and every spatially invariant admissible field, using the reference bound and its transfer allowance.

ns7-data-s056.Breakdown.Cert.ExtendedSupBoundHolds: The formal proposition specifies the resulting supremum estimate for inverse solutions, with the same period factor. It does not itself state the differentiated energy identity.

ns7-data-s057.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.IsHeld: The held correction has combined energy and coefficient norm at most $2\varepsilon$ and a gradient supremum bound $M$. Lean normalizes the coefficient weight to one and expresses the time bound as an essential supremum.

ns7-data-s060.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.small_fi: The strict inequality $2c_Lc_wM<1$ is the first smallness condition. Together with the energy budget, it is used to keep the correction within the ball of radius $2\varepsilon$.
ns7-data-s060.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.small_se: Equation (7.26) charges the weight, reference form, forcing and inverse bounds against $M^2$, with the whole budget multiplied by $4\varepsilon^2$. Lean writes the three terms involving $2S_{\max}/m$ separately.
ns7-data-s060.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.small_th: Equation (7.27) charges residual size, the quadratic contribution and the forcing contribution against the gradient budget $M^2$. The residual terms are multiplied by $4S_{\max}\varepsilon/m$.

ns7-data-s061.Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldContractsHold: The paper says its later argument does not use (7.26). The formal fixed-parameter contraction proof does use that scalar budget to control differences.

ns7-data-s063.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.params: `Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.params` uses exactly a selected coordinate subset, interval radii and a complementary scaled ball.
ns7-data-s063.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.scale_ne: Every coordinate scale is required to be nonzero.

ns7-data-s064.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.params: The parameter set constrains each selected coordinate by its own interval radius and puts the scaled complementary coordinates in a Euclidean ball. The nonnegative radii and nonzero scales used later yield compactness and convexity.

ns7-data-s065.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.frame_un: The formal matrix is invertible. Its column pairing is the transpose matrix action.

ns7-data-s066.Breakdown.Held.testSetZero_of: The displayed update occurs in this proof. The theorem’s conclusion is the existence of a zero for a continuous coefficient map satisfying both enclosures.

ns7-data-s067.Breakdown.Held.testSetZero_of: `Breakdown.Held.testSetZero_of` uses that update with a fixed invertible matrix and nonzero scales. It makes no differentiability assumption and does not claim an actual inverse Jacobian.

ns7-data-s068.Breakdown.Held.testSetZero_of: `Breakdown.Held.testSetZero_of` proves invariance of the parameter set from those two enclosures and then a zero. The derivation of the enclosures from the perturbation equation is a separate step.

ns7-data-s069.Breakdown.Cert.ExtendedAdjointEnclosureH: For the coordinates in $\mathcal J$, pairing the held equation with each chosen adjoint yields a separate scalar bound. The combined energy and forcing-coefficient budget controls the linear pairing and the error in the actuator vector together.
ns7-data-s069.Breakdown.Cert.ExtendedStiffEnclosureHol: For the coordinates outside $\mathcal J$, the bound uses the Euclidean norm of the projected force shift. The operator norm bound for the projected frame turns the force coefficient allowance into the ball radius estimate.

ns7-data-s070.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.adjoint_: The formal hypothesis imposes a uniform spatial $L^2$ bound at every time and parameter, which is stronger than period-square-integrability alone.
ns7-data-s070.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.adjoin: No continuity in the parameter is required of the adjoint family.
ns7-data-s070.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.coupli: The coupling matrices are arbitrary functions of the parameter without a continuity requirement.

ns7-data-s071.Breakdown.periodPairing: For each actuator $b_i$, the period pairing computes $\langle b_i,\psi_{\alpha,j}\rangle_{\mathcal H}$. Collecting these scalars over $i$ gives the vector in (7.31).
ns7-data-s071.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.actuat: The actuator error vector has entries $\langle b_i,\psi_{\alpha,j}\rangle_{\mathcal H}-(V_j)_i$. Its scalar product with the force coefficient vector produces the error bounded in (7.35).

ns7-data-s072.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.adjoint_: For each selected adjoint and admissible perturbation, the pairing of $(v\cdot\nabla)v$ with $\psi_{\alpha,j}$ is bounded in absolute value by $\tilde a_j\|v\|_w^2$. In Lean the convection term is the supplied weak gradient applied to $v$.

For each selected adjoint, subtract the $j$th coordinate of $Y(\alpha)\ell(v)$ from the pairing with a square-integrable periodic right-hand side. The residual is bounded by $a_j\|v\|_w$, with the linearized equation understood modulo a gradient.

Equation (7.34) bounds the difference between the adjusted force coefficient and $d_j\alpha_j$ by $o_j$. The adjustment subtracts both the adjoint pairing of the approximate residual and the prescribed correction constraint.

Equation (7.35) adds the quadratic allowance $\tilde a_j(2\varepsilon)^2$, the joint bound on the linear and actuator errors, and the offset $o_j$. Their sum must fit inside $|d_j|\varrho_j$ for each selected coordinate.
ns7-data-s072.Breakdown.Cert.extendedAdjointPairingHol: The pairing theorem proves the solenoidal consequence of the zero-perturbation case of the adjoint estimate.
ns7-data-s072.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.adjust: The adjusted multiplier starts with the frame pairing $V_j\cdot\beta^{\mathrm a}(\alpha)$ and subtracts the adjoint residual pairing and the constraint term $(Y(\alpha)\bar\ell(\alpha))_j$. The offset condition separately compares this quantity to $d_j\alpha_j$.

ns7-data-s073.Breakdown.Cert.ExtendedAdjointEnclosureH: `Breakdown.Cert.ExtendedAdjointEnclosureHolds` already replaces $V_j$ for the force-pairing vector and combines the linear, quadratic and discrepancy errors into the bound at radius $2\varepsilon$.

ns7-data-s074.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.actuat: The vector paired with $\beta$ is $\langle b,\psi_{\alpha,j}\rangle_{\mathcal H}-V_j$. This explains why approximating the adjoint pairings by the column $V_j$ makes the actuator error small.

ns7-data-s076.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.stiff_no: The first bound in (7.36) is an operator norm bound on the force coefficient vector projected to coordinates outside $\mathcal J$. Lean writes it as a comparison of squared Euclidean norms with constant $a_*^2$.
ns7-data-s076.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.stiff_of: The second bound in (7.36) takes the Euclidean norm of the complementary-coordinate differences $V_j\cdot\beta^{\mathrm a}(\alpha)-d_j\alpha_j$. That norm must be at most $o_*$ for every admissible parameter.
ns7-data-s076.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.stiff_in: Equation (7.37) requires $2\varepsilon a_*/\omega+o_*\le\varrho_*$. The first term bounds the allowed shift of the force coefficients, and the second allows for the offset already present at the approximate profile.

ns7-data-s077.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.params: The dimension may be zero and the interval/ball set need not have interior.
ns7-data-s077.Breakdown.rowNorm: With zero rows the finite sum and seminorm are zero.

ns7-data-s078.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData: The data structure takes the period, approximate profile, adjoints, residual and related terms as functions of the parameter. Appendix B supplies one way to represent those functions by finite data.

pdf-item-theorem-7-1.Breakdown.extended_certificate_orbit_pro: `Breakdown.extended_certificate_orbit_proved` turns the formal extended certificate into a nonzero weak recurrent profile. The companion theorem supplies the smooth profile at the selected period with its prescribed symmetries and correction bounds under the formal certificate hypotheses.
pdf-item-theorem-7-1.Breakdown.FarField.periodicLerayProfileE: `Breakdown.FarField.periodicLerayProfileExists_of_weak` gives existence of a smooth recurrent profile from a weak one. The statement does not retain the certificate parameter or identify its correction and symmetries.
pdf-item-theorem-7-1.Breakdown.Cert.extendedExistsZeroHeldHol: `Breakdown.Cert.extendedExistsZeroHeldHolds_of` adds $\beta+\beta^{\mathrm a}(\alpha)=0$ to the bounded-correction condition after normalization. Restoration of $\omega$ and identification with the same smooth profile are not conclusions of this row.
pdf-item-theorem-7-1.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.IsHeld: `Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.IsHeldSolution` gives the unit-weight joint bound, the constraints and an essential time supremum for a correction represented through the free inverse. The displayed formula concerns the continuous correction to the final smooth profile and the original weight $\omega$.
pdf-item-theorem-7-1.Breakdown.IsPerturbation: `Breakdown.IsPerturbation` requires the prescribed symmetries of the correction almost everywhere in space-time. (7.39) requires every prescribed symmetry pointwise for the final smooth profile.
pdf-item-theorem-7-1.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.profile_: The certificate requires the approximate velocity at each admissible parameter to satisfy the prescribed orthogonal actions and time shifts pointwise. The conclusion in Theorem 7.1 concerns those symmetries for the final corrected profile.
pdf-item-theorem-7-1.Breakdown.Cert.extendedSigmaProfileOfHel: `Breakdown.Cert.extendedSigmaProfileOfHeldHolds_of` gives existence of a weak unit-period field. It does not record the full prescribed symmetry set or a pointwise symmetry assertion for a smooth representative.

s7-4-correction.Breakdown.Cert.extendedExistsZeroHeldHol: After normalization `Breakdown.Cert.extendedExistsZeroHeldHolds_of` selects a parameter and a bounded correction with zero total forcing. It does not identify that correction with the difference between the final smooth profile and $W^{\mathrm a}_\alpha$.

pdf-item-equation-7-38.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.IsHeld: `Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.IsHeldSolution` gives the unit-weight joint bound, the constraints and an essential time supremum for a correction represented through the free inverse. The displayed formula concerns the continuous correction to the final smooth profile and the original weight $\omega$.
pdf-item-equation-7-38.Breakdown.Cert.extendedExistsZeroHeldHol: `Breakdown.Cert.extendedExistsZeroHeldHolds_of` adds $\beta+\beta^{\mathrm a}(\alpha)=0$ to the bounded-correction condition after normalization. Restoration of $\omega$ and identification with the same smooth profile are not conclusions of this row.

pdf-item-equation-7-39.Breakdown.IsPerturbation: `Breakdown.IsPerturbation` requires the prescribed symmetries of the correction almost everywhere in space-time. (7.39) requires every prescribed symmetry pointwise for the final smooth profile.
pdf-item-equation-7-39.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.profile_: Here the certificate’s invariance field applies to the approximate velocity, with time normalized by the period. To conclude (7.39) for the corrected smooth velocity, the correction must preserve the symmetries and they must pass to the smooth representative.
pdf-item-equation-7-39.Breakdown.Cert.extendedSigmaProfileOfHel: `Breakdown.Cert.extendedSigmaProfileOfHeldHolds_of` gives existence of a weak unit-period field. It does not record the full prescribed symmetry set or a pointwise symmetry assertion for a smooth representative.

pdf-item-theorem-7-2.Breakdown.extended_certificate_breakdown: `Breakdown.extended_certificate_breakdown_on_space` uses the formal extended certificate to exclude global smooth bounded-energy evolution for smooth compactly supported solenoidal data on $\mathbb R^3$. The same-profile quantitative trajectory in the corollary requires the additional companion theorem.
pdf-item-theorem-7-2.Breakdown.FarField.breakdownOnTorus_of_w: `Breakdown.FarField.breakdownOnTorus_of_weak` starts from existence of a weak recurrent profile and excludes global smooth evolution with periodic velocity for suitable periodic data. The conclusion allows nonperiodic pressure. It does not produce the quantitative torus trajectory in the paper.

pdf-item-theorem-7-3.Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExist: The definition can express recurrence with $P=\theta_0S>0$ and a given $R$. It does not prove that the already chosen profile has that recurrence, including the half-period case.

s7-4-remark-half-period.Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExist: The definition can express recurrence with $P=\theta_0S>0$ and a given $R$. It does not prove that the already chosen profile has that recurrence, including the half-period case.

s7-linear-p01-02.Breakdown.WeakProfile.physicalCurve: Let $S>0$ and let $v$ take values in $X=\dot H^1_{\rm div}(\mathbb R^3)$. For $t<1$, choose the formal time origin $s_0=0$ and the curve $x(s)=v(s/S)$. `Breakdown.WeakProfile.physicalCurve` then gives exactly $u(t)=D_{1/(1-t)}v(\theta)$ with $S\theta=-\log(1-t)$. For a general $s_0$, it gives the corresponding translate in similarity time.

s7-linear-p01-03.Breakdown.WeakProfile.physicalIdentity_o: `Breakdown.WeakProfile.physicalIdentity_of_parts` is the nonlinear weak equation for a bounded Sobolev curve on $(-1,1)$. It does not state the separate distributional free-operator and Laplacian identities displayed in (7.41) on $(-\infty,1)$.

s7-linear-p02-01.Breakdown.Cert.freePerturbationHolds_of: `Breakdown.Cert.freePerturbationHolds_of` constructs an admissible perturbation from invariant solenoidal forcing and identifies its weak free equation. This does not assert solenoidality of the free residual of every given $v\in\mathcal D_S$.
`Breakdown.Cert.Internal.FreeEnergyLocal.exists_energyCurve` provides a continuous periodic $X$-valued representative and integrated energy identity for the constructed free solution. The paper quantifies over all $v\in\mathcal D_S$ and states the differentiated identity.
s7-linear-p02-01.Breakdown.Cert.freeEnergyLocalHolds_of: `Breakdown.Cert.freeEnergyLocalHolds_of` gives a continuous scalar energy and its interval identity for the constructed inverse. Local absolute continuity and the almost-everywhere derivative are read from that identity.
s7-linear-p02-01.Breakdown.Cert.Internal.FreeInv.period_i: `Breakdown.Cert.Internal.FreeInv.period_identity` derives the equality in (7.43) from a period energy identity, with the stored second component representing $-\Delta v$. That identity is its hypothesis.
s7-linear-p02-01.Breakdown.Cert.freeInvHolds_of: The free inverse of a solenoidal source has a square-integrable Laplacian and gradient controlled by the source norm. Lemma 7.4 also starts from an arbitrary admissible perturbation and identifies its free operator as a solenoidal field.

`Breakdown.Cert.Internal.FreeEnergyLocal.exists_energyCurve` provides a continuous periodic $X$-valued representative and integrated energy identity for the constructed free solution. The paper quantifies over all $v\in\mathcal D_S$ and states the differentiated identity.
s7-linear-p02-02.Breakdown.Cert.freeEnergyLocalHolds_of: `Breakdown.Cert.freeEnergyLocalHolds_of` gives a continuous scalar energy and its interval identity for the constructed inverse. Local absolute continuity and the almost-everywhere derivative are read from that identity.

s7-linear-p02-03.Breakdown.Cert.Internal.FreeInv.period_i: `Breakdown.Cert.Internal.FreeInv.period_identity` derives the equality in (7.43) from a period energy identity, with the stored second component representing $-\Delta v$. That identity is its hypothesis.
s7-linear-p02-03.Breakdown.Cert.freeInvHolds_of: For the constructed free inverse, the squared Laplacian norm plus one quarter of the squared gradient norm is bounded by the squared norm of the source. The equality with the forcing pairing in (7.43) uses the period energy identity.

s7-linear-p03-01.Breakdown.Cert.freePerturbationHolds_of: `Breakdown.Cert.freePerturbationHolds_of` constructs a weak free solution from a solenoidal forcing. The paper proves by the divergence identity that the residual of every admissible perturbation is solenoidal. The stated formal implication runs in a different direction.

`Breakdown.Cert.Internal.FreeEnergyLocal.IsEnergyCurve` requires a continuous energy curve that agrees almost everywhere with the frequency trace of the constructed inverse. The passage uses that representative to discuss energy at each time.

b12-allowed-symmetries.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.GeneratedByC: `Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.GeneratedByClassSymmetries` writes every allowed pair with angle $a\pi/\kappa$, optional $R_*$ and time shift $a/2+j$, with $a$ a nonnegative integer and $j$ an integer.

pdf-item-equation-B-2.Breakdown.CertCell.labelPhase: For a natural azimuthal order $\kappa$, an integer label $\iota=(\iota_1,\iota_2)$, and real $\theta,\phi$, `Breakdown.CertCell.labelPhase` is $E_\iota(\theta,\phi)=\exp(i[2\pi(2\iota_2-\iota_1)\theta+\kappa\iota_1\phi])$. This is exactly (B.2), with the same sign and normalization. The paper uses $\kappa\ge3$. The definition also makes sense for other natural $\kappa$. The arithmetic characterization of all invariant integer frequencies is a separate assertion following the equation.

b12-harmonic-parity.Breakdown.CertCell.labelPhase: The formula supplies the claimed frequencies and hence the invariance. The converse arithmetic characterization is a separate consequence of the integer label parametrization.

b12-first-symmetry.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.fieldClass: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.fieldClassInvariant_holds` proves the symmetry for the prescribed finite divergence-free representation under its spline and phase conditions. The paper sentence describes arbitrary combinations with meridian coefficients.

b12-label-reflection.Breakdown.CertCell.labelFlip: Reflection reverses the azimuthal frequency and preserves the time frequency, giving the stated harmonic identity.

pdf-item-equation-B-3.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.chartCoord: The formula and range agree under $L>0$. The definition is also total for other lengths, which the shape assumptions exclude.
pdf-item-equation-B-3.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.heightRat: The formula agrees away from the origin. `Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.heightRatio` additionally assigns $\eta(0)=0$ by zero division.

pdf-item-equation-B-4.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.polarVecQ: `Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.polarVecQ` therefore extends the coordinate formula beyond its usual domain. At nonzero points it has the weighted polar-vector interpretation in the paper. That interpretation supplies no value at the origin.
pdf-item-equation-B-4.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.azimVecQ: For $y\ne0$, `Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.azimVecQ` gives $a(y)=(-y_2/|y|,y_1/|y|,0)$, the azimuthal vector in (B.4). Its zero-denominator convention gives $a(0)=0$, so the vector vanishes on the entire $y_3$ axis.

b12-weighted-unit-vectors.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.polarVecQ: At nonzero points the coordinate formula is the polar unit vector times $\sqrt{1-\eta^2}$. At the origin the total definition instead gives $p(0)=-e_3$, so the coordinate interpretation has no origin value.
b12-weighted-unit-vectors.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.azimVecQ: Away from the origin the formula is the azimuthal unit vector times $\sqrt{1-\eta^2}$. Its assigned origin value is zero.

b12-phase-condition.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsRadialPh: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsRadialPhase` gives $C^3$ regularity on $(-\delta,\infty)$ for some $\delta>0$ and one bound for $sf'$, $s^2f''$ and $s^3f'''$ on $s\ge0$. It does not require $f$ itself to be bounded.

pdf-item-equation-B-5.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.keyPhase: The same time, azimuthal and radial phases are added inside one complex exponential. The axis uses an assigned angular value.
pdf-item-equation-B-5.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shiftedSca: On the physical coordinate range $\sigma<1$, substitution $|y|=L\sigma/(1-\sigma)$ gives exactly this first-order operator.

pdf-item-equation-B-6.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shapeInfoF: For every real $\theta$ and $y\in\mathbb R^3$, the formal field is the componentwise real part of $\sum_{(\iota,l)\in\mathcal A}E_\iota(\theta,\phi(y))\exp(ilf(|y|^2))[u_0y/|y|+u_1p+u_2a]$, with $\sigma=|y|/(|y|+L)$, $\eta=y_3/|y|$ and the amplitudes of (B.7)–(B.8). This is the finite-sum formula (B.6). Quotients by zero and the angular coordinate on the axis are assigned zero. The definition itself imposes no joining, symmetry, divergence or decay condition.
pdf-item-equation-B-6.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.keyDiverge: Under the full phase and spline hypotheses `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.keyDivergenceFree_closed` proves divergence freedom of every present mode. It does not define the finite summation itself.
pdf-item-equation-B-6.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsTimeFiel: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsTimeFieldData` gives admissibility conditions for the finite harmonic data used in (B.6). It requires closure of the mode set under negation and reflection, the corresponding conjugation and parity of the amplitudes, specified polynomial joins and lower bounds on the decay exponents. The field itself is evaluated by another definition.

b12-finite-mode-data.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shapeInfoF: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shapeInfoField` uses a finite subset of integer labels and phase indices and the three amplitudes. The divergence identity is a separate theorem.
b12-finite-mode-data.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.keyDiverge: Under the full phase and spline hypotheses `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.keyDivergenceFree_closed` proves divergence freedom of every present mode. It does not define the finite summation itself.

b12-nonzero-exponents.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsTimeFiel: For a nonzero azimuthal label, the active polynomial amplitudes are $A$ and $B$. Their exponent bounds are $h_0\ge2$ and $h\ge1$, as required for the behavior at the coordinate boundaries.

pdf-item-equation-B-7.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.reducedCom: In the branch $\iota_1\ne0$ the factors, derivative, signs and divisor $\kappa\iota_1$ match. Positive $\kappa$ ensures that divisor is nonzero.
pdf-item-equation-B-7.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsTimeFiel: The amplitude condition for $\iota_1\ne0$ requires the piecewise polynomials $A,B$ and the exponent bounds $h_0\ge2$, $h\ge1$. Evaluating the three components of (B.7) uses the separate component definition.

b12-zero-stream.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.reducedCom: The zero-azimuthal branch forms this stream expression from a complex $\gamma$, the real origin function and $S$. The natural decay bound $h\ge1$ is imposed on its data.

pdf-item-equation-B-8.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.reducedCom: The zero-azimuthal branch forms this stream expression from a complex $\gamma$, the real origin function and $S$. The natural decay bound $h\ge1$ is imposed on its data.
pdf-item-equation-B-8.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsOriginPr: The condition matches through two derivatives when $\sigma_g<1$. If $\sigma_g=1$ it imposes no matching beyond 1, which lies outside the physical range $\sigma<1$.

b12-origin-function.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsOriginPr: The condition matches through two derivatives when $\sigma_g<1$. If $\sigma_g=1$ it imposes no matching beyond 1, which lies outside the physical range $\sigma<1$.

b12-zero-divergence.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.keyDiverge: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.keyDivergenceFree_closed` proves zero divergence at every spatial point, including the axis and origin, under the full amplitude and phase hypotheses. The displayed calculation uses spherical coordinates off the origin.

b12-field-data-description.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shapeInfoF: The finite data supply the harmonic labels, polynomial amplitudes, exponents and radial shape parameters. The field is obtained by evaluating their finite complex harmonic sum and taking its componentwise real part.

adapted.N5-20.1.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsJoinedSp: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsJoinedSpline` requires neighboring polynomial pieces to have equal traces and equal normal derivatives on their shared coordinate line. These conditions justify gluing the pieces across that edge.

b12-c1-periodic.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.FieldJoint: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.FieldJointSmooth` is precisely the joint $C^1$ and normalized time-periodicity conclusion under the stated finite-data and shape hypotheses.

b12-second-derivatives.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.FieldWeakH: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.FieldWeakHessian` identifies the supplied second derivative distributionally. It does not itself prove the bound or the printed description of its classical values off the interfaces.
b12-second-derivatives.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.fi: The order theorem bounds the supplied weak second derivative, hence gives boundedness at order $h_*=1$. The exact interface description is a separate fact.

b12-conjugation.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsTimeFiel: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsTimeFieldData` requires negated label and phase index, conjugate active amplitudes and equal exponents. The active amplitudes are $A,B$ for nonzero azimuthal modes and $S,T,\gamma$ for zero azimuthal modes.

b12-reflection-data.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsTimeFiel: The reflected nonzero modes use $A(\sigma,-\eta)$ and $-B(\sigma,-\eta)$. The zero-mode stream and swirl are odd.

b12-both-symmetries.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.fieldClass: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.fieldClassInvariant_holds` proves the reflection and twisted half-period identities for the represented field, with the same coefficient hypotheses.

b12-gamma-invariant.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.GeneratedByC: `Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.GeneratedByClassSymmetries` gives the representation of each element of $\Gamma$. Invariance also uses the field symmetry and period-one theorems.

b12-axis-factors.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.reducedCom: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.reducedComps` contains exactly these powers. Their vanishing and differentiability at the axis and origin require the corresponding analytic estimates.

b12-axis-zero-mode.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.polarVecQ: The polar vector vanishes on the axis away from the origin, but its total definition gives $p(0)=-e_3$. The paper sentence needs that origin qualification.
b12-axis-zero-mode.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.azimVecQ: The weighted azimuthal vector vanishes on the entire axis, including its assigned zero value at the origin.

b12-decay-orders.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.fi: For a natural number $h_*$ bounded above by every mode exponent, `Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.fieldDecayOrder_holds` gives all four decay estimates with one constant, including the time derivative.

b12-decay-one.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.fi: Taking the permitted natural order equal to 1 gives the orders 1,2,3 used in (7.8), together with a time-derivative bound.

b12-profile-dependence.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Pr: The profile combines the amplitudes for $W_\alpha^0$ and $W_\alpha^i$ affinely after replacing the common phase by $f+(k\cdot\alpha)f_*$.

b12-phase-cutoff.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.st: `Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.stepPhase_holds` assumes precisely a $C^2$ polynomial cutoff with a breakpoint strictly between 0 and 1, zero below it and equal to 1 near the outer endpoint.

pdf-item-equation-B-9.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Pr: The profile is the sum $W_\alpha^0+\sum_i\alpha_i W_\alpha^i$ evaluated at the parameter-dependent phase. The constituent fields can depend on $\alpha$ through that phase.
pdf-item-equation-B-9.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.mo: The phase substitution is exactly $f+af_*$ with $a=k\cdot\alpha$, while length and azimuthal order are unchanged.
pdf-item-equation-B-9.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.st: The formal upper limit is $\sqrt s$ at input $s$. Setting $s=|y|^2$ gives $|y|$. The cutoff removes the apparent singularity at $\rho=0$.
pdf-item-equation-B-9.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.af: The definition is affine when its phase is fixed. Agreement of the phase and derivative terms on the closed ball is an additional fact.
pdf-item-equation-B-9.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.st: `Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.stepPhase_holds` proves zero for every squared radius $s\le r_\chi^2$, including the closed ball in the paper.
pdf-item-equation-B-9.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.In: `Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Internal.stepPhase_tail` gives $R>0$ and $C$ with $f_*(s)=C+(\log s)/2$ for $s>R^2$, which is the stated $\log|y|$ tail after $s=|y|^2$.

b12-independent-amplitudes.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Pr: The amplitude data for $W_\alpha^0$ and $W_\alpha^i$ are fixed independently of $\alpha$, share length and phase, and retain separate mode sets, splines and origin functions.

b12-period-affine.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Is: The reciprocal period is required to be affine on $\mathcal K$. Its constant term equals $1/S(0)$ when $0\in\mathcal K$.

b12-forcing-affine.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Is: Each forcing coordinate is required to equal its central value plus the stated real linear combination on $\mathcal K$.

adapted.N5-22.1.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Pr: `Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.PressureShapeEntry.pressure` defines the represented pressure as the center contribution plus a parameter-weighted sum of the tangent contributions. The passage identifies the pressure convention for the residual after shifting by half the squared speed.

The representation uses endpoint derivatives of orders below the chosen depth and finitely many interior coefficients. The tensor product gives each rectangular polynomial.

b12-forcing-data.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsCompactT: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsCompactTimeFieldData` requires vanishing pieces and $\gamma=0$, but allows the cutoff to precede a partition edge. The exact breakpoint condition in the paper is imposed separately for the support radius.

b12-forcing-smooth.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.FieldJoint: A forcing field satisfying the full amplitude and shape conditions has the asserted $C^1$ regularity, including the origin and axis.

b12-forcing-divergence.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.keyDiverge: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.keyDivergenceFree_closed` gives zero divergence of each mode and hence of the finite real sum. The $\Gamma$ symmetry is supplied separately.
b12-forcing-divergence.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.fieldClass: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.fieldClassInvariant_holds` gives the two generating symmetries. Full $\Gamma$ invariance additionally uses the description of every element of $\Gamma$ and time periodicity.

b12-forcing-support.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.compactFie: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.compactFieldSupportRadius_holds` gives vanishing for strict inequality and assumes the cutoff is a breakpoint in each active partition. Continuity supplies the boundary case.

b12-adjoint-data.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Is: The condition fixes the same field for every parameter, with a common length, phase and origin function and decay exponent at least 3.

b12-adjoint-rows.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Ad: Only rows $j\in\mathcal J$ are required to equal fixed coefficients for all $\alpha\in\mathcal K$. Other rows are unrestricted by this identification.

b12-cell-rectangle.Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.IsCellBo: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.IsCellBox` imposes the same strict endpoint orders, and the associated solid uses the absolute height to include both halves.

b12-mesh-cover.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ActuatorSu: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ActuatorSupportFacts` supplies the square cover and forcing support radii. Validity and disjointness of the cell interiors are separate mesh assumptions.

b12-tensor-polys.Breakdown.CertCell.CellMatField.field: The tensor definition assembles the stated cell polynomials and harmonics. Finite label closure and complex conjugation are separate conditions.

pdf-item-equation-B-10.Breakdown.pinValue: The tensor-gradient integral is the same after identifying output-first formal matrix entry $(b,a)$ with the paper coefficient $\Xi_{ab}$.
pdf-item-equation-B-10.Breakdown.CertCell.CellMatField.field: The formal matrix uses output index first, so its entry $(b,a)$ corresponds to the paper coefficient $\Xi_{ab}$. This supplies the tensor in (B.10). The separate tensor-gradient integral defines $\ell_i(v)$. Closure of the label sets and conjugation conditions are additional hypotheses.

b12-tensor-reflection.Breakdown.CertCell.CellMatField.field: The reflected label, reflected height and product of cylindrical-frame signs give exactly the stated sign rule.

b12-tensor-support.Breakdown.CertCell.CellMatField.field: Vanishing outside the cells is built into the indicator sum. Boundedness follows only with finitely many valid bounded cells and polynomial coefficients.

b12-zero-pin-gap.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Is: The target is identified with the approximate profile constraint, making the prescribed correction constraint exactly zero.

b12-phi-representation.Breakdown.PotentialShape.cylField: The cylindrical potential definition is the real sum of the specified harmonic times $r$ times an endpoint-derivative polynomial spline.

b12-phi-error.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.AdjointDefectBou: `Breakdown.AdjointDefect.AdjointDefectBounded.pin_round` is the squared integral version for every real coefficient vector, with nonnegativity of $c_\Xi$ required separately.

b12-row-polynomial-data.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsRowValues: The row-data condition requires complex polynomial triples with real coefficients in the zero harmonic, on each specified cell.

b12-row-divergence.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsRowValues: The row-data condition requires the same polynomial divergence identity and the two axis vanishing conditions. It does not assert divergence freedom after discontinuous zero extension.

b12-row-gram.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsRowValues: Positive definiteness is imposed on the complex polynomial Gram matrix with the cylindrical measure $r\,dr\,dz$ for every tested cell and label.

b12-row-realfields.Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.rowFieldOf: The row construction starts from these real and imaginary cell generators with the reflected signs, then mixes them by the real Gram inverse square root.

pdf-item-equation-B-11.Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.rowFieldOf: The formal field is the unit row $G^{-1/2}\tilde e$. The factor $\sqrt{\tau_k}$ is kept in a separate positive row weight, giving the same weighted pairing seminorm.
pdf-item-equation-B-11.Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.rowWeightOf: The separate formal weight is the cell-and-label test weight divided by $c$. The printed cap follows when $c=3/50$ and the required test-weight bound is imposed.
pdf-item-equation-B-11.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.rowFieldsOrt: `Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.rowFieldsOrthonormal` proves inner products $\delta_{kl}$ for normalized rows, assuming positivity of the assembled Gram matrix. Rescaling by $\sqrt\tau$ gives the paper norms.

b12-row-cap.Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.rowWeightOf: The separate formal weight is the cell-and-label test weight divided by $c$. The printed cap follows when $c=3/50$ and the required test-weight bound is imposed.

b12-row-orthogonality.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.rowFieldsOrt: `Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.rowFieldsOrthonormal` proves inner products $\delta_{kl}$ for normalized rows, assuming positivity of the assembled Gram matrix. Rescaling by $\sqrt\tau$ gives the paper norms.

adapted.N5-15.1.Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.extendedCoerciveC: Under the represented piece-data hypotheses, `Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.extendedCoerciveClause_of_pieceData_proved` obtains the weighted coercive inequality for admissible weak perturbations. pdf-item-equation-B-12.Breakdown.modeVel: The formal Fourier index is $(j,j')=(2\iota_2-\iota_1,\kappa\iota_1)$, in normalized time $\theta$ and azimuth $\phi$, with this substitution the inverse-rotation average, conjugation and factor $1/(2\pi)$ agree.
pdf-item-equation-B-12.Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.ClassSupportHo: For the admitted weak perturbation class `Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.ClassSupportHolds` gives almost-everywhere vanishing of velocity, gradient and Hessian modes outside this lattice. b12-harmonic-support.Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.ClassSupportHo: For the admitted weak perturbation class `Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.ClassSupportHolds` gives almost-everywhere vanishing of velocity, gradient and Hessian modes outside this lattice. pdf-item-equation-B-13.Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.modeShiftRotat: `Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.modeShiftRotate` proves this identity for a period-one field and an integrable orbit at the point concerned. The paper leaves those analytic hypotheses implicit in its phrase “a field”.

adapted.N5-27.1.Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.IsAdmissibleWeak: `Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.IsAdmissibleWeak` includes finiteness of the selected harmonic classes and bounds on their weights. These assumptions control the sums used to define the multiplier.

adapted.N5-28.1.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsJoinedScal: `Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsJoinedScalar` uses a common partition and requires reflected normal derivatives to match with sign $(-1)^j$ in order $j$. b12-sign-definition.Breakdown.PieceWeights.sgn: For the disjoint sets required here, `Breakdown.PieceWeights.sgn` gives the three values of the paper’s sign function. If both labels are present, it gives priority to membership of $\iota$ in $\mathcal N_p$.

pdf-item-equation-B-15.Breakdown.PieceWeights.frameFreq: Substituting the physical integer pair $(2\iota_2-\iota_1,\kappa\iota_1)$ gives the same frequency. Positivity of $S$ excludes the definition’s zero-division case.

b12-mu-seminorm.Breakdown.PieceWeights.seminormSq: The quantity is the extended nonnegative sum of the stated weighted squares. Restricting the all-integer frequency sum to the symmetry lattice gives the paper form.

adapted.N5-30.1.Breakdown.PieceWeights.modeDensity: `Breakdown.PieceWeights.modeDensity` combines the five weighted quantities from a mode’s velocity, gradient and second derivatives and their curl components. Its coefficients depend on the frequencies and weights specified in the passage.

adapted.N5-31.1.Breakdown.PieceWeights.modeTerm: `Breakdown.PieceWeights.modeTerm` evaluates the mode density on the five derivative and velocity norms of one harmonic. The resulting expression contains both the positive frequency contribution and the weighted errors.

pdf-item-equation-B-18.Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.stretchFormWith: The three terms, signs and factor $1/2$ agree. `Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.stretchFormWith` uses the actual first derivative of the reference and its supplied weak second derivative.

adapted.N5-32.1.Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.densityNegWith: `Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.densityNegWith` takes the negative part of the density before summing and integrating it as an extended nonnegative quantity. The positive part is handled by the corresponding separate definition.

pdf-item-equation-B-19.Breakdown.CertCell.InstanceSplit.Enclosu: The two $\lambda$ sums and the quadratic $\mu$ inequality have the same factors and quantifiers. The condition explicitly requires $n_\mu\ge0$.
pdf-item-equation-B-19.Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.IsAdmissibleWeak: The analytic condition includes the pointwise reference and transport bounds, a positive frequency lower bound on each selected set, and nonnegativity of $I'_2$, together with the regularity and decay assumptions.

b12-prop-b1-hypotheses.Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.pieceMultiplierDe: `Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.pieceMultiplierDensityWeakHolds_proof` admits measurable periodic perturbations with weak derivatives and square-integrable transport and right-hand side. b12-prop-b1-existence.Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.pieceMultiplierDe: `Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.pieceMultiplierDensityWeakHolds_proof` supplies the finite $\mu$ seminorm and one solenoidal $L^2$ multiplier satisfying the test identity, under the full weak analytic hypotheses.

b12-prop-b1-norm.Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.pieceMultiplierDe: With $c=3/50$, the formal constant $(1+n_\lambda+n_{\nabla\lambda}/\sqrt{w_0})^2/c+n_\mu/c_\mu$ is exactly the displayed $c_M^2$. $w_0$ is the positive lower bound on $w$.

b12-prop-b1-finiteness.Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.pieceMultiplierDe: The nonnegative-integral inequality and a finite scalar right-hand side imply this exact finiteness conclusion when $I^-$ is finite.

pdf-item-equation-B-20.Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.pieceMultiplierDe: The nonnegative-integral inequality and a finite scalar right-hand side imply this exact finiteness conclusion when $I^-$ is finite.

b12-laplacian-pairing.Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.EnergyIdentitySmo: `Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.EnergyIdentitySmoothWeakHolds` agrees, but its smooth-stage formal assertion explicitly adds weighted $L^2$ and higher derivative integrability hypotheses, and uses a supplied weak Hessian for the $C^1$ reference.

adapted.N5-36.1.Breakdown.Coercive.curlWeightIdentityDec: `Breakdown.Coercive.curlWeightIdentityDecayHolds_proof` proves the weighted curl identity with decay and derivative hypotheses that justify removing the cutoff after integration by parts. adapted.N5-37.1.Breakdown.Coercive.smoothApproximationHo: `Breakdown.Coercive.smoothApproximationHolds_proof` supplies smooth solenoidal periodic approximants and the convergence of derivatives and weighted norms needed to pass to admissible weak perturbations. The passage explains how convolution respects the symmetry.

pdf-item-equation-B-21.Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.RowRestClause: With $c=3/50$ and $t=1000$, `Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.RowRestClause` is the same lower bound, represented with separate positive and negative integrals and including $I^-<\infty$.
pdf-item-equation-B-21.Breakdown.CertCell.rowRestClause_closed: The cell theorem derives this remaining lower bound from the complete cell, represented-field and assembly assumptions. It is conditional on those same finite data.

pdf-item-equation-B-22.Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.extendedCoerciveC: `Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.extendedCoerciveClause_of_rowMultiplierInequality` uses $c_M/\sqrt c\le c_1$ and $\sqrt{t/c}\le c_2$, which specialize to the first two inequalities. It does not impose the row-norm budget for $c_0$.
pdf-item-equation-B-22.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsRowInstanc: `Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsRowInstance` gives the row budget $c_0\ge0$ and $T/c\le c_0^2$. b12-lemma-b2.Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.extendedCoerciveC: `Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.extendedCoerciveClause_of_pieceData_proved` gives the same coercive estimate for the larger periodic weak perturbation class, explicitly assuming admissible weights, the remaining density condition and the two scalar budgets for every $\alpha\in\mathcal K$.
b12-lemma-b2.Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.rowMultiplierIneq: The theorem performs the cancellation after proving finiteness and obtains the displayed squared inequality with the same nonnegative $\mu$ term and row/constraint remainder.

b12-lemma-b2.Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.extendedCoerciveC: Positivity of $c$ permits division by $\sqrt c$, and the two coefficient budgets give exactly the final constants. The values $c=3/50$ and $t=1000$ recover this line.

adapted.N5-39.1.Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.extendedCoerciveC: `Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.extendedCoerciveClause_of_rowMultiplierInequality` combines the multiplier and row bounds after establishing finiteness of the integrals. That permits real subtraction of the positive and negative parts and cancellation of the shared density integral.

ns-b3-quarter-plane.Breakdown.CertCell.modeDensityBridge_clo: `Breakdown.CertCell.modeDensityBridge_closed` first proves two separate identities for positive and negative densities. Their signed difference gives the expression to be divided into cells and exterior.

ns-b3-modal-meridian-values.Breakdown.CertCell.modeDensityBridge_clo: `Breakdown.CertCell.modeDensityBridge_closed` uses rotation and time-shift laws to reduce each modal density to its value at time zero on the meridian.
