ns-b3-mean.Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.meanStr: The normalization is exactly one time period and the angular mean with factor $1/(2\pi)$.

pdf-item-theorem-B-3.Breakdown.CertCell.modeDensityBridge_clo: `Breakdown.CertCell.modeDensityBridge_closed` gives the positive and negative $4\pi$ identities separately, even when they are infinite. The signed equality follows when the negative part is finite.

ns-b3-b3-hypotheses.Breakdown.CertCell.modeDensityBridge_clo: For every periodic weak perturbation it proves the identities (B.23) for the positive parts and for the negative parts separately, with no finiteness hypothesis. Finite $\mathcal I^-$ is needed to pass to the paper's signed equation.

pdf-item-equation-B-23.Breakdown.CertCell.modeDensityBridge_clo: `Breakdown.CertCell.modeDensityBridge_closed` gives the positive and negative $4\pi$ identities separately, even when they are infinite. The signed equality follows when the negative part is finite.

ns-b3-b3-integrability.Breakdown.CertCell.DensityIdentity: `Breakdown.CertCell.DensityIdentity` identifies the two nonnegative integrals separately. Finiteness on the quarter plane follows from the corresponding finite space and time integral.

adapted.N6-02.1.Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.halfPlaneReduc: `Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.halfPlaneReduction` reduces the integral of nonnegative harmonic contributions to the half-plane using reflection, angular symmetry and relabeling of the modes. It can be applied to the positive and negative parts individually because the sign is taken before averaging.

ns-b3-cylindrical-factor.Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.halfPlaneReduc: `Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.halfPlaneReduction` combines cylindrical integration with reflection to give the factor $4\pi$. The factor $2\pi$ before reflection is one step of its proof.

ns-b3-reflection-change-of-variable.Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.modeFlip: `Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.modeFlip` assumes the reflection belongs to the symmetry set and concludes the reflected mode identities. The rotation relation and change of angular variable are steps of its proof, rather than separate conclusions.

pdf-item-equation-B-24.Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.modeFlip: The velocity clause is this reflection identity almost everywhere. `Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.modeFlip` also gives the gradient and Hessian reflection identities.

ns-b3-reflect-stretch.Breakdown.CertCell.modeDensityBridge_clo: The formal proof uses invariance of the stretching expression and of its positive and negative angular means. `Breakdown.CertCell.modeDensityBridge_closed` records the resulting integral identities.

ns-b3-positive-negative.Breakdown.CertCell.modeDensityBridge_clo: `Breakdown.CertCell.modeDensityBridge_closed` keeps the time and angle means of the positive and negative parts separately, avoiding a subtraction of infinite integrals.

ns-b3-stretch-bounded.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.exteriorPoin: The formal inequality bounds the mean stretching by a sum of modal majorants on the exterior. Couplings between modes are accounted for in that sum.

ns-b3-b25.Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.supremum: The bound adds the strain loss, the mean vorticity-gradient contribution and the oscillatory vorticity-gradient contribution. The last term uses the balancing length to split a mixed product into gradient and velocity squares. Both vorticity-gradient coefficients use $\sqrt{7/2}$.

ns-b3-curl-matrix.Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.supremum: The formal gradient has output index first, so its curl vector has the opposite sign from this printed vector under the same entry order. A transposed gradient convention reconciles them, and the squared norm used in the majorant is identical in either convention.

ns-b3-stretch-coefficients.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsRegionChar: `Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsRegionChargeBound` has the same strain and mean and oscillatory vorticity-gradient bounds at every time and angle. It permits $s_1,s_2,s_3$ to depend on the harmonic, whereas the paper uses common functions of $(r,z)$. The positive balancing length $h$ must be common in both.

ns-b3-stretch-signs.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsRegionChar: The condition explicitly includes nonnegativity of the two operator-norm bounds. Nonnegativity of the strain bound also uses the separate trace-zero consequence of divergence-freeness.

ns-b3-axis-modes.Breakdown.CertCell.IsCellMesh: The axis-cell clause allows only lattice labels with first component zero among the resolved harmonics.

ns-b3-degrees.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsCellMo: The layout condition imposes $d_0\ge1$ and identifies the side and volume degrees. The mesh gives $d\ge d_0+2$ and $d_0\ge2$ for tested modes.
ns-b3-degrees.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsTestOf: The test-shape condition gives exactly the three componentwise degree bounds, using natural-number $q=d_0$. The restrictions on the two degrees belong to the mesh and layout conditions.

ns-b3-cell-data.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsCellMo: The formal layout includes the named polynomial and boundary data together with their linear relations and a parametrization. Existence of the corresponding weak traces is established by the cell estimates.

ns-b3-additional-unknowns.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsCellFo: The local inequality quantifies real $\beta$ and $\zeta$ and arbitrary complex auxiliary entries along with the harmonic data. It imposes an inequality on these entries rather than merely listing them.

adapted.N6-06.1.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.TreeRowCondi: `Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.TreeRowConditions` constrains the cell embeddings and the global quadratic form on one vector of slaved and free coordinates. It records that the free-coordinate map vanishes while the global form still accounts for the free variables.

ns-b3-global-relations.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.TreeRowCondi: Every used local row must be justified by the prescribed trace, symmetry, divergence or gauge relations before the embedding can be used.

ns-b3-complex-forms.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.TreeStateInt: The formal assembly identity takes $\operatorname{Re}(x^* A x)$ for each complex local matrix and expresses the resulting real quadratic values in real global coordinates. This agrees with the paper’s real-part convention and does not require every local matrix in the identity to be Hermitian.

ns-b3-leaf-matrix.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsLeafVa: For each resolved harmonic `Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsLeafValues` gives positive $I_2$ and nonnegative $I'_2$ lower bounds and a bounded measurable Hermitian form on nine gradient and three velocity entries.

ns-b3-leaf-coefficients.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsLeafVa: The formal clauses bound both highest-order coefficients below on every point of the cell for each resolved harmonic.

ns-b3-leaf-upper-lower.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsLeafVa: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsLeafValues` spells out constant model and pairing penalties and the cell radial weight. These are the explicit allowances summarized by the paper as constants or constant multiples of $1/r$.

ns-b3-b26-admitted-vectors.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.InRowRange: The formal permitted vectors include the stated global row values and also pressure-gauge and constant-pressure directions. Separate conditions make those additions invisible to the quadratic form.

pdf-item-equation-B-26.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.EliminationC: The formal comparison has these five contributions but applies on the admitted local vectors, including pressure-gauge directions. It also imposes the positivity and row conditions needed for elimination.

ns-b3-b27.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.hessTailGain: In the Hessian estimate, the gain on the unresolved part is the smaller radial or vertical eigenvalue at the next degree, with the radial weight and the frequency penalty with shift two. The scalar allocation of that gain to the cell error is a further condition.
ns-b3-b27.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.TailBudget.H: `Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.TailBudget.Holds` requires the explicit sum of gradient, curl, velocity and model-error allowances to fit within this Hessian threshold. The display specifies only the available threshold.

The formal factor equals one exactly when the inner radius is zero and equals that radius otherwise.

ns-b3-polynomial-eigenvalues.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.hessTailGain: The Hessian tail gain uses the smaller radial and vertical eigenvalues at $Q+1$, the first degree beyond the retained polynomials. The radial eigenvalue uses $j(j+2)$ on an axis cell and $j(j+1)$ off the axis. The angular contribution uses shift two.

ns-b3-unresolved-charges.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.offModeDensi: The density definition accepts the constant and three charge functions as inputs. Their boundedness and nonnegativity on the exterior are imposed by separate region conditions.

ns-b3-b28.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.offModeDensi: The formal density subtracts the stretching majorant and the curl, gradient and velocity charges before evaluating the mode.

ns-b3-modified-stretch-constant.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef.wi: The coefficient transformation uses the supplied $\mathsf c^*$ in both stretching terms, yielding the replacement specified here.

ns-b3-rectangle-region.Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.IsCreditPatch: The rectangle condition gives positive inner radius, width and height. Its inclusion in the cell union is an additional condition identifying rectangle moments with cell data.

ns-b3-rectangle-test.Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.IsCreditPatch: `Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.IsCreditPatch` adds positive upper and lower charge bounds, Lipschitz test functions and a nonoverlapping boundary segmentation to the Dirichlet-form and inverse-matrix comparisons.

ns-b3-regional-test.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.IsOffModeCon: The condition tests an unresolved density on one measurable region and one set of harmonics by uniform scalar coefficient bounds.

ns-b3-region-coefficient-data.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.IsOffModeCon: The formal pointwise condition gives a region, harmonic set, coefficient bounds and splitting function. The alternative using four exterior constants is a separate condition.
ns-b3-region-coefficient-data.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.IsExteriorCo: The formal exterior condition supplies the four constants and geometric Hardy hypotheses for regions reaching infinity.

ns-b3-regional-cover.Breakdown.CertCell.rowRestClause_closed: The assembly uses coverage of each cell by its local regions and coverage of the exterior by its own regions, with intersections in null sets. These hypotheses justify summing the regional integral bounds over the full domain.

ns-b3-charged-coefficients.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef.wi: For an original cross coefficient zero, the transformation gives exactly these six coefficients after subtracting the stretching and other charges.

ns-b3-effective-coefficients.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef.gr: The effective gradient coefficient adds twice the negative part in the signed form $2\min(f'_1+f'_2(k_0-1)_+^2/r^2,0)$ and the Hessian gain $f_2(k_0-2)_+^2/r^2$ to $f_1$. The nonnegative shifted velocity coefficient is a separate quantity.
ns-b3-effective-coefficients.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef.ve: The velocity coefficient adds $t(k_0-1)_+^2/r^2$ to $f_0$. This credits the part of the angular gradient estimate bought with the amount $t$ removed from the gradient coefficient.

ns-b3-b29.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef.Pa: The test makes the Hessian and shifted velocity coefficients nonnegative. It takes $t\ge0$ from the effective gradient coefficient $f_1^*$ and requires $f_{01}^2\le4(f_1^*-t)f_0^*$. This is the condition that controls the mixed product by the remaining gradient and velocity squares.

ns-b3-exterior-shapes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.IsExteriorCo: The formal ray radius is also required to be measurable, homogeneous, bounded above and bounded away from zero. The square alternative requires zero azimuthal frequency.
ns-b3-exterior-shapes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.IsDirectionR: The directional-radius condition adds measurability, a strictly positive uniform lower bound and a finite uniform upper bound to dependence on direction.

ns-b3-exterior-integrated-test.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.IsExteriorCo: `Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.IsExteriorCondition` combines pointwise lower bounds on the coefficients with an integrated Hardy estimate. It does not require the unresolved density itself to be pointwise nonnegative on these exteriors.

ns-b3-exterior-coefficient-bounds.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.IsExteriorCo: The formal exterior condition includes exactly the nonnegative Hessian floor, effective gradient floor and the inverse-square and inverse-radius ceilings listed here.

pdf-item-equation-B-30.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.IsExteriorCo: `Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.IsExteriorCondition` includes these scalar inequalities together with the coefficient bounds, harmonic restrictions and measurable uniformly bounded positive ray radius.

ns-b3-b31.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.modeRayInver: The formal ray theorem gives the largest displayed modal constant $1/4+(|\kappa\iota_1|-1)_+^2$, under measurable positive bounded directional-radius assumptions.
ns-b3-b31.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.modeSquareIn: For the zero azimuthal mode with reflection symmetry, the formal approximation theorem gives this inequality with $\Lambda_0=2$ on the square exterior, assuming the smooth component estimates.

pdf-item-theorem-B-4.Breakdown.CertCell.formNegFinite: `Breakdown.CertCell.formNegFinite` isolates uniform lower coefficient bounds and reference-field regularity and decay as sufficient hypotheses for this finiteness conclusion. It does not require all the subsequent matrix conditions.

ns-b3-b4-finite.Breakdown.CertCell.formNegFinite: `Breakdown.CertCell.formNegFinite` isolates uniform lower coefficient bounds and reference-field regularity and decay as sufficient hypotheses for this finiteness conclusion. It does not require all the subsequent matrix conditions.

ns-b3-b32.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.exteriorPoin: `Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.exteriorPointBound_of_tripleSum` is this almost-everywhere exterior bound by the sum of modal stretching majorants.

ns-b3-b4-global-state.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.TreeRowCondi: The formal row condition supplies compatible determined coordinates and a zero base perturbation, while the analytic construction from a perturbation is carried out in the assembly proof.

ns-b3-b33-error-quantifiers.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsCellFo: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsCellFormBound` quantifies all real $\beta$ and $\zeta$ and complex auxiliary values, then uses explicit cell contributions. It has no existential quantifier over four numbers $r_0,\ldots,r_3$, and the global coordinate construction is a separate step.

pdf-item-equation-B-33.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsCellFo: The formal local inequality uses fixed row, pairing, gradient-slack and rectangle contributions with a symmetric pressure gradient, and compares positive and negative integrals. It does not introduce four existential error numbers.

ns-b3-b33-absolute-convergence.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsCellFo: The local inequality is expressed using nonnegative positive and negative sums. Its statement does not itself assert the absolute convergence printed here.

ns-b3-b34.Breakdown.CertCell.InstancePair.pairShar: `Breakdown.CertCell.InstancePair.pairSharesFromSurrogateProfiles_holds` supplies the actuator and constraint pairings with their allocated approximation errors.
ns-b3-b34.Breakdown.CertCell.creditLeavesBound_clo: This estimate controls the rectangle forms that enter the error bound with factor two. The cell forcing-row terms and the actuator and constraint pairing errors enter through separate estimates.

ns-b3-square-final-claim.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.modeSquareIn: The formal implication proves the constant-two bound for weak zero-azimuthal modes with the required reflection identity, from the smooth component estimates.

ns-b3-negative-finite-proof.Breakdown.CertCell.formNegFinite: `Breakdown.CertCell.formNegFinite` uses lower coefficient bounds, weighted velocity control from Hardy, and reference-field derivative decay to show that the negative integral is finite.

adapted.N6-10.1.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.exteriorPoin: `Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.exteriorPointBound_of_tripleSum` combines the separate bounds on exterior stretching terms to give the pointwise bound. This is the estimate obtained in the paper by splitting the products with Young’s inequality.

ns-b3-resolved-energy-bound.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsLeafVa: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsLeafValues` gives the pointwise matrix upper bound and highest-order coefficient floors. The integrated resolved-mode estimate additionally uses the polynomial projection identities.

ns-b3-coupling-label-rule.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.meanStretchT: Each reference label $\alpha$ couples perturbation labels $\iota$ and $\iota-\alpha$ in the formal harmonic sum.

ns-b3-resolved-model-coupling.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.EliminationC: The formal matrix comparison uses the retained polynomial coupling matrix as supplied data. Its relation to the reference field is an additional model-error bound.

ns-b3-eliminated-mode.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.EliminationC:
The formal elimination requires $k
e0$ and $k^2
e1$ for $k=\kappa\iota_1$, together with positive weights. In the appendix $\kappa\ge3$, so the paper’s $\iota_1
e0$ gives both frequency exclusions.

ns-b3-unresolved-absorption.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsLeafVa: The local Hermitian-form lower bound controls the stretching of the remainder up to explicit allowances. The unresolved density separately subtracts the charged terms.
ns-b3-unresolved-absorption.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.offModeDensi: `Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.offModeDensity` records exactly the charged terms subtracted from each unresolved modal density. Nonnegativity uses the regional tests.

ns-b3-forcing-rows.Breakdown.CertCell.rowSharesOfInstance: `Breakdown.CertCell.rowSharesOfInstance` identifies the sum of the resulting row contributions with the forcing seminorm. The cell integration by parts is an earlier step in obtaining those rows.

ns-b3-row-and-pairing-errors.Breakdown.CertCell.rowSharesOfInstance: The cell shares sum to the forcing-row contribution $3[F]^2/(50\cdot4\pi)$. The signed terms pairing the modes with actuator and pin gradients are handled separately.
ns-b3-row-and-pairing-errors.Breakdown.CertCell.InstancePair.pairShar: `Breakdown.CertCell.InstancePair.pairSharesFromSurrogateProfiles_holds` gives the actuator and constraint contributions and their explicit gradient and coefficient error allowances, replacing the paper’s four error variables.

ns-b3-rectangle-absorption.Breakdown.CertCell.creditLeavesBound_clo: The formal rectangle bound uses the reflected and conjugate modes to control twice the moment form by allocated velocity energies.

ns-b3-b34-sum.Breakdown.CertCell.rowSharesOfInstance: Summing the cell shares recovers the forcing-row penalty $3[F]^2/(50\cdot4\pi)$. The actuator and constraint pairings and their approximation errors enter through separate estimates.
ns-b3-b34-sum.Breakdown.CertCell.InstancePair.pairShar: `Breakdown.CertCell.InstancePair.pairSharesFromSurrogateProfiles_holds` bounds the summed actuator and constraint part.
ns-b3-b34-sum.Breakdown.CertCell.creditLeavesBound_clo: `Breakdown.CertCell.creditLeavesBound_closed` bounds the summed rectangle contribution. All three are needed for (B.34).

ns-b3-square-component-argument.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.squareExteri: `Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.squareExteriorSmoothStatement` proves the two scalar constant-two estimates for real compactly supported $C^1$ functions vanishing on the required coordinate line. Completing squares and integration by parts occur in its proof.
ns-b3-square-component-argument.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.modeSquareIn: The theorem lifts the componentwise exterior Hardy estimates for smooth fields to weak modes. The axial component uses vanishing at the reflection plane, and the transverse components use vanishing at the axis. The completing-square estimates for the smooth components enter as a premise.

pdf-item-theorem-B-5.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.angularModeB: The theorem bounds the angular contribution for the mode and its curl, at both zero and first derivative order. It uses $k=\kappa\iota_1$ and the Frobenius norm on derivative matrices, with the inequalities holding almost everywhere.

ns-b3-b35.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.angularModeB: For a weak mode of frequency $k=\kappa\iota_1$, angular differentiation supplies inverse-radius bounds for the velocity, gradient, curl and curl gradient. The four inequalities hold almost everywhere and use the Frobenius norm for derivative matrices.

ns-b3-b36-hypotheses.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.pointwiseQua: The formal scalar theorem takes coefficient domination, a nonnegative actual gradient-of-curl coefficient, the angular inequalities and the full scalar test as premises. These give the printed intermediate lower bound within its proof. `Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.pointwiseQuadraticTest` is the later nonnegativity assertion.

pdf-item-equation-B-36.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef.gr: `Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef.gradFloor` gives the exact effective coefficient $f_1^*$. It does not alone assert the density inequality.
pdf-item-equation-B-36.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.Internal.Ext: The available exterior lower-bound theorem replaces $f_1^*$, $f_0$ and $f_{01}$ by an exterior constant and inverse-radius bounds. It is a later specialization of this estimate, not its exact statement.

ns-b3-b5-conclusion.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.offModeCondi: Under the coefficient bounds and (B.29), `Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.offModeConditionSound_holds` gives almost-everywhere nonnegativity on the region.

ns-b3-curl-differences.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.AngularRelat: The algebraic condition includes the resulting curl-size inequality. Its elementary derivation from component differences is a proof step.

ns-b3-angular-derivative.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.angularModeB: `Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.angularModeBounds` states the resulting almost-everywhere angular inequality for weak modes. The displayed differentiated symmetry is used in the proof and is not a separate conclusion of this theorem.

ns-b3-gradient-commutator.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.angularModeB: `Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.angularModeBounds` gives the Hessian angular gain with shift two. Its proof derives it from the two rotation actions on the gradient. The commutator identity is not its stated conclusion.

ns-b3-curl-angular.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.angularModeB: The formal angular theorem includes the same shift-one estimate for the curl and its gradient.

ns-b3-lower-coefficients.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.pointwiseQua: The scalar theorem assumes coefficient domination and nonnegativity of the actual gradient-of-curl coefficient. Admissible multiplier weights provide those premises for the mode.

ns-b3-intermediate-curl-gain.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.pointwiseQua: This intermediate inequality is established by the separate coefficient and curl-gain comparisons in the formal proof. `Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.pointwiseQuadraticTest` states their consequence after the additional scalar nonnegativity test, rather than this intermediate density bound.

ns-b3-scalar-minimum.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.pointwiseQua: The proof of the scalar theorem carries out these angular and minimum-with-zero bounds, but its conclusion is nonnegativity after the additional discriminant test.

ns-b3-discriminant.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.pointwiseQua: The formal proof transfers the nonnegative splitting term to velocity and applies the nonnegative quadratic-form test exactly as described.

pdf-item-theorem-B-6.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.modeRayInver: `Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.modeRayInverseSquare` additionally requires the directional radius to be measurable, uniformly positive and bounded above. It yields the modal Hardy constant before lowering it to $\Lambda_0$.
pdf-item-theorem-B-6.Breakdown.CertCell.exteriorConditionSoun: `Breakdown.CertCell.exteriorConditionSound_closed` turns the exterior coefficient and angular bounds into an integral estimate for the admissible perturbations. The proof uses finite gradient energy and Hardy control. The stated real integral uses Lean’s conversion from nonnegative integrals, so ordinary signed integration also needs finiteness of the negative part, which the paper states explicitly.

ns-b3-b6-ray-claim.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.modeRayInver: `Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.modeRayInverseSquare` additionally requires the directional radius to be measurable, uniformly positive and bounded above. It yields the modal Hardy constant before lowering it to $\Lambda_0$.

ns-b3-b6-integrated-claim.Breakdown.CertCell.exteriorConditionSoun: `Breakdown.CertCell.exteriorConditionSound_closed` is a comparison of the negative and positive extended integrals. It does not include the printed negative-part finiteness as a separate conclusion. It uses finite gradient and Hardy bounds.

ns-b3-ray-density-class.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.radialRay: The formal radial theorem is stated for $L^6$ real fields with square-integrable weak gradient on a measurable ray exterior. Applying it to both components of a mode yields this proof step.

adapted.N6-14.1.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.radialRay: `Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.radialRay` integrates along rays with a measurable axis-dependent cutoff that scales coherently on each ray and has a positive bounded radius on unit directions. Thus the exterior part of a ray is an interval beyond its cutoff.

ns-b3-angular-radial-combination.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.modeRayInver: The formal proof adds the radial quarter-constant and the squared angular gain, using orthogonality of the radial and azimuthal directions.

ns-b3-exterior-coefficient-signs.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.Internal.Ext: The formal scalar lemma assumes the nonnegative exterior constants and the strict positivity of $\Lambda_0$, then proves nonnegativity and absorption of the two coefficients produced by Young’s inequality.

ns-b3-exterior-lower-bound.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.Internal.Ext: The lower bound uses a constant times $|\nabla u|^2$ and subtracts two losses, one proportional to $|u|^2/\rho^2$ and one proportional to $|\nabla u|\,|u|/\rho$. A separate scalar inequality absorbs the mixed loss.
The formal Young inequality, with $s=\sqrt{\Lambda_0}$, gives exactly the second step, transferring the mixed product to the gradient and velocity squares.

adapted.N6-16.1.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.signedTre: `Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.signedTreeLowerBound` sums the node inequalities, keeping positive pivot terms and the losses from column terms. When a child’s outgoing form enters its parent with opposite sign, those intermediate forms cancel.

ns-b3-attached-matrices.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.TreeStateInt: The formal total-form identity uses the global matrix, all embedded cell blocks, doubled rectangle forms and cancelling pairs of auxiliary matrices.

ns-b3-b38.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.TreeStateInt: The total quadratic value adds the global form, the local cell forms pulled back to global coordinates and twice the rectangle contributions. The forms passed between nodes cancel in this sum.

ns-b3-node-data.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.PassesRea: `Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.PassesRealNodeEnclosure` gives real symmetric input and output models, nonnegative symmetric error matrices, positive row weights and the prescribed pivot and column data.

ns-b3-b39.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.PassesRea: The field `input_lower` bounds the input quadratic form by the node’s assigned form plus its children’s contributions and the error form on $|x|$. The field `front_upper` bounds the form passed to the parent by the base form after deducting the nonpivot diagonal allowances and adding the second error form. Both comparisons hold for every real $x$.

ns-b3-b40.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.PassesRea: The field `row_bound` adds the two entrywise error allowances to the absolute residual in each row. It weights each entry by $\mathsf w_i/\mathsf w_j$ and requires the sum in row $i$ to stay within $\mathsf m_i$. The two quadratic form enclosures are separate fields.

ns-b3-pivot-diagonal-and-slack.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.PassesRea: `Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.PassesRealNodeEnclosure` uses a diagonal supported on the pivot set. Its slack allowance $\underline{\mathsf p}_{\xi,j}$ is at most $\mathsf p_j-\mathsf m_j$ at each pivot $j$.

ns-b3-complex-coordinates.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.PassesCom: The formal coordinates have one optional real entry and one optional real multiple of an imaginary entry. The pivot restrictions are imposed separately.

ns-b3-complex-matrices.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.PassesCom: The complex condition uses Hermitian matrices $H$ and $K$, real nonnegative error matrices, coordinate-wise weights and radii, and a finite pivot-coordinate set.

ns-b3-complex-node-enclosures.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.PassesCom: The first enclosure bounds the scaled Hermitian input by the real node and child forms plus the scaled error on $|\mathsf z|$. ns-b3-complex-residual.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.PassesCom: The residual uses conjugate transposes and entrywise complex moduli, with the positive row weights on the complex coordinates.

ns-b3-complex-pivot-transfer.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.PassesCom: The enclosure assigns signs $\pm1$ to the real pivot coordinates and requires them to be distinct. It sums the real-coordinate lower bounds for each complex pivot. The real and imaginary negative columns are assigned injectively.

pdf-item-theorem-B-7.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.signedTre: The formal lower bound retains the root’s passed quadratic form. Dropping it under the nonnegativity hypothesis yields the displayed inequality.
pdf-item-theorem-B-7.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.pivotCoun: `Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.pivotCountPositive` concludes that there exists a real subspace of dimension at least the number of determined coordinates on which the root expression $\langle V_{\rm root}x,x\rangle+\sum_{\xi,j}\underline p_{\xi,j}x_j^2-\sum_\xi|Y_\xi^Tx|^2$ is strictly positive for every nonzero vector. In the proof the subspace is exactly the common kernel of the column pairings. Its stated conclusion records existence and the dimension bound, rather than naming that kernel. The lower bound comparing the root expression with $N$ is a separate theorem.

ns-b3-b41.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.signedTre: The formal lower bound retains the root’s passed quadratic form. Dropping it under the nonnegativity hypothesis yields the displayed inequality.

ns-b3-column-kernel-positive.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.pivotCoun: The stated conclusion gives existence of a positive subspace for the root expression with the required dimension. Its proof chooses the common column kernel. The tree lower bound then transfers positivity to $\mathsf N$.

ns-b3-exterior-loss-comparison.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.offModeDensi: `Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.offModeDensity` identifies the removed charges. Their nonnegative signs and $c_*\ge\sqrt{7/2}$ imply the comparison with the uncharged exterior majorant.

ns-b3-exterior-sum-positive.Breakdown.CertCell.exteriorConditionSoun: The formal regional exterior theorem gives the signed-part comparison for each exterior test. The passage to the whole complement and the harmonic sum additionally uses covering, no positive-area overlap, and finiteness.
ns-b3-exterior-sum-positive.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.exteriorPoin: The formal mean-stretching bound is the other ingredient in concluding nonnegativity of the full exterior contribution.

ns-b3-sum-before-b44.Breakdown.CertCell.initialState_closed: The assembly combines the cell, rectangle, exterior and global inequalities. It has already used $2\zeta\cdot\ell(v)-|\zeta|^2/t\le t|\ell(v)|^2$, so the conclusion corresponds to the upper bound after completing the square.

pdf-item-equation-B-44.Breakdown.CertCell.initialState_closed: `Breakdown.CertCell.initialState_closed` gives the global matrix upper bound after using $2\zeta\cdot\ell(v)-|\zeta|^2/t\le t|\ell(v)|^2$. pdf-item-equation-B-44.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.TreeStateInt: `Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.TreeStateInternal.quadValue_totalForm_eq` identifies the quadratic form of the assembled matrix as the sum of the cell, rectangle and global forms. ns-b3-find-free-coordinate.Breakdown.CertCell.stateEnclosureCertifi: The formal terminal theorem concludes nonnegativity of the scalar density gap through the finite-dimensional argument, without returning the chosen free vector as its conclusion.

adapted.N6-20.1.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.pivotCoun: `Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.pivotCountPositive` takes the common kernel of the column pairings and uses rank–nullity to bound its dimension from below in terms of the column count. pdf-item-equation-B-45.Breakdown.sixthPowerGradientBound_four_t: The same constant follows by taking square roots. `Breakdown.sixthPowerGradientBound_four_thirds` applies to any $L^6$ vector field with weak $L^2$ gradient, without solenoidality.

pdf-item-equation-B-46.Breakdown.CertReduction.energyBoundsHold: `Breakdown.CertReduction.energyBoundsHolds_proof` gives constant-weight spatial supremum estimates and a period gradient-energy bound. pdf-item-theorem-B-9.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.ShiftNumbersBo: `Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.ShiftNumbersBounded` records four bounds for the changes from reference to center and from center to actual profile. They are uniform pointwise bounds and time-uniform $L^2$ and $L^3$ bounds on the respective gradient changes. The first and third budgets in (B.48) belong here. The two estimates of Lemma B.9 use further hypotheses.
pdf-item-theorem-B-9.Breakdown.CertReduction.FrozenFormBounde: `Breakdown.CertReduction.FrozenFormBounded` records the lower bound $-s_-I$ on the reference strain and the $L^3$ bound $n_{\mathrm r}^{(3)}$ on the reference gradient, with budget $s_-/w_*+n_{\mathrm r}^{(3)}/\sqrt{3w_*}\le c'_3$. These are premises for the reference-form estimate in Lemma B.9.
pdf-item-theorem-B-9.Breakdown.CertReduction.gapTransferBridg: `Breakdown.CertReduction.gapTransferBridgeHolds_proof` bounds the change in the spacetime convection operator by the weighted energy of a perturbation. Its hypotheses bound separately supplied summands of the velocity and gradient differences in $L^\infty$ and $L^2$ or $L^3$. The paper uses velocity differences and their actual gradients as those summands.
pdf-item-theorem-B-9.Breakdown.CertReduction.formShiftBridgeH: `Breakdown.CertReduction.formShiftBridgeHolds_proof` bounds the change in the spatial energy form when replacing the reference field by the actual one. It uses $w_*>0$, regularity and decay of those fields, and bounds on the split velocity and gradient differences. The separate spacetime convection estimate uses a different declaration.
pdf-item-theorem-B-9.Breakdown.CertReduction.frozenFormBridge: `Breakdown.CertReduction.frozenFormBridgeHolds_of_convection` bounds the spatial form from below for the regular, decaying reference field. The nonnegative strain and $L^3$ gradient allowances enter through the middle budget in (B.48). The shift from the reference to the actual profile is a further step.

pdf-item-equation-B-47.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.ShiftNumbersBo: `Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.ShiftNumbersBounded` supplies the first four bounds, with operator norms of the gradients and uniform quantification in time and parameter.
pdf-item-equation-B-47.Breakdown.CertReduction.FrozenFormBounde: `Breakdown.CertReduction.FrozenFormBounded` supplies the reference-gradient $L^3$ bound and the lower bound for the reference strain. The four profile differences are separate.

ns-b4-006.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.ShiftNumbersBo: The formal difference bounds hold at every real time and every spatial point, and the gradient norms are taken on $\mathbb R^3$.
ns-b4-006.Breakdown.CertReduction.FrozenFormBounde: The strain condition is quantified over every vector, so it is exactly a lower bound between quadratic forms.

pdf-item-equation-B-48.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.ShiftNumbersBo: The first and third scalar budgets are imposed, with the same factors $1/\sqrt{w_*}$ and $1/(2\sqrt{w_*})$.
pdf-item-equation-B-48.Breakdown.CertReduction.FrozenFormBounde: The middle scalar budget is imposed. The two profile-difference budgets are separate.

ns-b4-008.Breakdown.CertReduction.gapTransferBridg: `Breakdown.CertReduction.gapTransferBridgeHolds_proof` gives the squared spacetime bound for the change in convection. ns-b4-008.Breakdown.CertReduction.formShiftBridgeH: `Breakdown.CertReduction.formShiftBridgeHolds_proof` bounds the change of the spatial form by $c_3''$. The reference lower bound is a separate input.
ns-b4-008.Breakdown.CertReduction.frozenFormBridge: `Breakdown.CertReduction.frozenFormBridgeHolds_of_convection` gives the reference lower bound with $c_3'$, assuming the transport integration-by-parts identity. Adding the form-change estimate gives the stated $c_3$.

ns-b4-009.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.ShiftNumbersBo: The two changes are $W_0^{\mathrm a}-W^{\mathrm r}$ and $W_\alpha^{\mathrm a}-W_0^{\mathrm a}$. Adding them gives the full profile change. Lean takes separate bounds on each change and on its gradient to estimate the convection difference.

pdf-item-equation-B-49.Breakdown.CertReduction.gapSupTermHolds_: With $w_*>0$, a period-one weak perturbation $v$, and a coefficient $Z$ bounded by $s$, `Breakdown.CertReduction.gapSupTermHolds_proof` gives $\int_0^1\int|(Z\cdot\nabla)v|^2\le(s^2/w_*)E(v)$. The theorem uses the lower integral, which agrees with the squared $L^2$ norm when the coefficient is measurable.
pdf-item-equation-B-49.Breakdown.CertReduction.gapGradTermHolds: `Breakdown.CertReduction.gapGradTermHolds_proof` gives the $L^2$- and $L^3$-coefficient estimates after period integration. The printed statement consists of spatial inequalities.
pdf-item-equation-B-49.Breakdown.CertReduction.cubicWeightProdu: Hölder and the Sobolev constant $2/\sqrt3$ give the last coefficient estimate. The other two lines require separate bounds.

ns-b4-014.Breakdown.CertReduction.convectionIdenti: `Breakdown.CertReduction.convectionIdentity_holds` is the identity summed over the three velocity components after the divergence term has vanished. The printed line retains the componentwise intermediate term.

ns-b4-015.Breakdown.CertReduction.FrozenFormBounde: The quadratic-form assumption supplies the lower bound $-s_-|g|^2$ for every vector $g$.

It also has an $L^2$ alternative for $A$, with the coefficient $c_w/\sqrt{w_*}$ in place of $1/\sqrt{3w_*}$.

ns-b4-017.Breakdown.CertReduction.frozenFormBridge: `Breakdown.CertReduction.frozenFormBridgeHolds_of_convection` is the lower bound for the reference form under its strain, $L^3$ gradient and scalar-budget hypotheses.

ns-b4-018.Breakdown.CertReduction.shiftSupTermHold: `Breakdown.CertReduction.shiftSupTermHolds_proof` supplies the absolute integral estimate for the advecting-profile difference.
ns-b4-018.Breakdown.CertReduction.shiftGradTermHol: `Breakdown.CertReduction.shiftGradTermHolds_proof` supplies the $L^2$ and $L^3$ gradient-coefficient contributions to the absolute form difference.

The paper obtains the stronger absolute-value estimate on the difference by pairing the convection change with $\Delta u$.

ns-b4-019.Breakdown.CertReduction.formShiftBridgeH: `Breakdown.CertReduction.formShiftBridgeHolds_proof` supplies the contribution $c_3''$. It must be added to the reference bound.

pdf-item-theorem-B-10.Breakdown.CertReduction.adjointQuadCoeff: `Breakdown.CertReduction.adjointQuadCoeff` defines the two coefficient $2/(\sqrt3\,w_*)$ for the $L^3$ case and $c_w/\sqrt{w_*}$ for the $L^2$ case. The norm hypotheses are imposed separately.
pdf-item-theorem-B-10.Breakdown.CertReduction.adjointQuadratic: After the absolute pairing estimate and period integration facts are supplied, `Breakdown.CertReduction.adjointQuadraticBridge_of` is the same quadratic adjoint inequality.

ns-b4-025.Breakdown.CertReduction.adjointQuadratic: The final assembly uses the prescribed scalar budget and concludes (7.32).

ns-b4-027.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.DualBounded: `Breakdown.AdjointDefect.DualBounded` has the same sum of two nonnegative budgets, with the two parts listed in reverse order. It does not require exact periodicity of the ordinary part.

ns-b4-031.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.dualBoundedBound: The same pairing bound holds for a larger weak test class without periodicity or solenoidality. This theorem lists iterated-integrability conclusions and takes the two component pairing estimates as premises.

pdf-item-equation-B-50.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.AzimuthalParts.s: `Breakdown.AdjointDefect.AzimuthalParts.smoothModeInverseSquare` states the estimate for an angular projection of a smooth compactly supported real vector field. It does not state the weak scalar result directly.

Its pressure-gradient decay is encoded by $r|\nabla q|\le C$ and $r^3|\nabla q|\le C$, which gives the same near-origin and far-field orders away from $r=0$, up to changing the constant. These weighted inequalities do not restrict the derivative at the origin. The formal hypothesis therefore differs in the derivative requirements and in the precise decay bounds.

pdf-item-equation-B-52.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.adjointTransport: `Breakdown.AdjointDefect.adjointTransport` supplies the time, dilation and convection terms. The Laplacian, constraints and potentials are separate.
pdf-item-equation-B-52.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.AdjointDefectEnt: The formal flux uses the skew generator gradients. Its negative divergence equals the printed Laplacian terms when the generators are divergence-free.

ns-b4-049.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.AdjointDefectBou: The central residual has the same dual bound uniformly for every parameter, together with the potential norms.

ns-b4-050.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.AdjointDefectBou: With the fitted-direction set empty, the coordinate, positive-weight, weighted velocity, common dual and time-derivative bounds are exactly those imposed here.

ns-b4-054.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.representationHo: `Breakdown.AdjointDefect.representationHolds_of_density` uses the weak equation tested against solenoidal fields, and a decaying curl potential. It concludes the combined adjoint pairing identity.

ns-b4-059.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.Internal.Potenti: `Breakdown.AdjointDefect.Internal.PotentialBound.slice_identity` combines the justified flux, pressure and Laplacian integrations by parts under its sharper potential hypotheses. The compact constraint replacement is treated separately.

ns-b4-061.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.Internal.Potenti: `Breakdown.AdjointDefect.Internal.PotentialBound.slice_identity` supplies the potential line at each time. Parameter and constraint replacement terms are separate.

ns-b4-064.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.freeShiftBoundHo: `Breakdown.AdjointDefect.freeShiftBoundHolds_proof` controls the two convection terms together with the weighted coefficient norm. The time-frequency term is separate.

ns-b4-078.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.ba: `Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.ballAgreement_holds` proves agreement of the represented fields and listed derivatives inside the open ball. It uses the phase vanishing and regularity conditions.

ns-b4-079.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.ba: `Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.ballAgreement_holds` lists agreement of velocity, spatial gradient, represented Hessian, pressure and pressure gradient in the ball.

ns-b4-080.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.In: At pressure differentiability points `Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Internal.OffsetBall.defect_expands` gives the ordered quadratic expansion. Summing the two orders off the diagonal gives this upper-triangular expression almost everywhere.

ns-b4-081.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.of: `Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.offsetBallIdentity_holds` is the interior pairing expansion. The exterior split, forcing identity and subtraction of $d_j\alpha_j$ are additional algebraic steps.

adapted.N6-31.1.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CertificateCla: `Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CertificateClauses` records the residual, scalar and matrix requirements that the construction takes directly as hypotheses, including the conditions cited in (7.9) and (7.23).

b4-prop-b14.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.isExtendedCert: `Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.isExtendedCertificate_of_parts` reaches the same certificate, with an existentially chosen decay constant, but takes ten of those analytic steps (among them the offset, profile-change and adjoint estimates) as explicit premises. The closed cell theorem tied to the sentence after this proof supplies them, so the two together assert what the paper proves.
b4-prop-b14.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCond: The formal hypothesis specifies fifteen groups for one consistent data set, including functional and representation conditions left unwritten in the paper. The full equivalence of the condition lists cannot be read from this sentence alone.

ns-b4-087.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.isExtendedCert: `Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.isExtendedCertificate_of_parts` supplies a common decay constant making these data a certificate and takes ten analytic implications as explicit premises. The final cell theorem supplies those premises.

adapted.N6-32.1.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.isExtendedCert: `Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.isExtendedCertificate_of_parts` assembles an extended certificate for the given data from the separate field, scalar and matrix hypotheses and the analytic implications. The closed cell result supplies those analytic implications.

adapted.N5-15.2.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.breakdownOnSpa: `Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.breakdownOnSpaceAndTorus_of_cell_system_condition` assumes a complete cell data set and proves both global nonexistence results. The same-profile quantitative whole-space estimates use the companion Lean. The quantitative periodic trajectory and verification of the fitted data are further obligations.

ns-b4-094.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCond: For the polynomial stretching groups the allowed constants are exactly $\sqrt{7/2}$ or $\sqrt{9/2}$, and the choice $\sqrt{7/2}$ carries the trace-zero condition. For the modes that are not resolved and for the exterior, the formal assumptions allow any stretching constant at least $\sqrt{7/2}$, so there these constants are lower bounds rather than fixed values.

adapted.N6-39.1.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shapeInfoF: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shapeInfoField` evaluates the encoded harmonic shape and takes its real part to represent a physical velocity field. The numerically chosen coefficients are data in the paper.

ac-048.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.fieldClass: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.fieldClassInvariant_holds` gives the same half-period rotation for admissible fields in the time coordinate $\theta=s/\bar S$, with angle $\pi/\varkappa$. The displayed instance additionally needs $\varkappa=19$, $\bar S>0$, and identification with the computed field.

adapted.N6-42.1.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.fi: `Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.fieldDecayOrder_holds` gives decay bounds for the modeled field and its derivatives under the polynomial degree and radial phase conditions. The passage specializes the decay powers to $h=1$. Numerical constants for the fitted field require the supplied coefficients and their bounds.

ac-051.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.fi: `Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.fieldDecayOrder_holds` gives an upper bound $C(1+|y|)^{-1}$ under the coefficient hypotheses. It gives neither a nonzero leading asymptotic coefficient nor the numerical constant for this field.

ac-049.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.logPhaseIs: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.logPhaseIsRadial` proves regularity and bounded scaled derivatives for this functional form when $r_c>0$, after setting its coefficient to $4\pi/\bar S$. It does not assert that the computed profile uses this phase.

ac-037.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.keyPhase: This equality follows from the general phase only after choosing order $19$, the printed logarithmic phase and $l=\iota_1-2\iota_2$. None of these choices is imposed by the definition.

ac-038.Breakdown.SimilarityResidual: `Breakdown.SimilarityResidual` uses advection, $-\Delta W$ and pressure $q$, and does not impose either equation. Smoothness, solenoidality and $H=q+|W|^2/2$ identify it with the printed residual.
ac-038.Breakdown.Coercive.Internal.TestDensityP: For smooth divergence-free $W$ `Breakdown.Coercive.Internal.TestDensityProof.negSsp_curl_curl` replaces the double curl by $-\Delta W$. It asserts neither the pressure equation nor vanishing of the residual.

ac-039.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.Internal.Rem: The matrix identity gives the advection/curl-cross difference. Identifying it with the kinetic-energy gradient also uses the chain rule for a differentiable field.

adapted.N6-46.1.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.defect_l: `Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.defect_l2` requires one bound on the $L^2$ norm of $F_\alpha^{\mathrm a}$ for every $\alpha\in\mathcal K$. The exploratory residual at the fitted parameter provides no such uniform estimate.
adapted.N6-46.1.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.defect_r: `Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.defect_rows` imposes the bounds on the specified residual row pairings for every $\alpha\in\mathcal K$. These uniform row bounds are an additional certificate input beyond the residual norm.

ac-043.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsStrong: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsStrongRightSide` states the continuum residual formula almost everywhere using the perturbation’s weak derivatives, the reference field, forcing and pressure gradient. Under the identification of those derivative slots, this is the linearized expression in the passage. The discretized derivative matrix is a separate object.
ac-043.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.coupling: If the supplied matrix is $\nabla v$, its curl represents $\operatorname{curl}v$. The coupling field then adds $(\operatorname{curl}v)\times W$ and $(\operatorname{curl}W)\times v$, the two first-order coupling terms of (C.2).
ac-043.Breakdown.Coercive.Internal.TestDensityP: For a smooth divergence-free perturbation `Breakdown.Coercive.Internal.TestDensityProof.negSsp_curl_curl` gives exactly the replacement of $-\Delta v$ by its double curl.

adapted.N6-52.1.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.af: `Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.affineField` forms the affine field from the center and the parameter-weighted tangent directions at fixed phase. In the ball where $f_*=0$, the varying-phase expression (B.9) agrees with this affine form.

adapted.N6-53.1.Breakdown.PieceWeights.frameFreq: `Breakdown.PieceWeights.frameFreq` computes $2\pi\iota_1/P+a\iota_2$ from the temporal harmonic, angular harmonic, period and frame rate. Substituting the two frame rates and their mode indices gives the frequencies displayed in the passage.
